records.title: Overview
records.description: What InputBooster is, the problem it solves, and the boundaries it deliberately keeps.
records.content: InputBooster is a client-side Minecraft mod that samples keyboard and mouse state faster than the game tick. It recovers a press that begins and ends between two ticks and turns it into the action vanilla would have run. It is not an autoclicker. Minecraft reads most gameplay input on the client tick. At 20 ticks per second, a tick is 50 ms long. A short tap can go down and up inside one tick window, especially at low FPS or during a stutter. Vanilla never sees the edge, so no attack, jump or use happens. InputBooster watches the platform key state between ticks and preserves that edge. The mod is client only . A server does not install it and does not need a companion plugin. The actions it drains end in ordinary vanilla client calls, so the server sees normal gameplay. InputBooster 4.1.2-alpha is the current source tree. Its input engine and settings screen are new code and have not been tested in a running client. 4.0.3-stable is the last stable build. Read Limitations before relying on a setting in competitive play. The problem in one tick Vanilla's keyboard and mouse handlers only tell the player what is true when the tick runs. If a key is already released by then, the press can be lost. Polling at 60–1000 Hz means the mod can observe the transition while it exists and queue one action for the next tick. E[InputEngine state machine] B[Keyboard events] --> E C[Mouse events] --> E E --> Q[Bounded queue / 128] Q --> D[InputDrainer at tick HEAD] D --> V[Vanilla client calls] D --> S[Suppress vanilla duplicate for that tick] } caption="The input path in 4.1.2-alpha. Vanilla's own handlers still run; the mod only adds another observer and a drain step." /> What it does Samples the player's actual bound keys at a configurable rate, from 60 to 1000 Hz. Uses keyboard and mouse event hooks as a second source when they are available. Converts state changes into one action per physical edge through a single state machine. Queues actions in a bounded 128-entry queue and drains them at the start of a client tick. Suppresses vanilla's duplicate attack or use for the tick the mod already handled. Provides optional combat, movement, overlay, profile and replay tools around that core. What it does not do It does not generate clicks or movement without a physical press. It does not extend reach, change hit registration, or alter what the server receives. It does not replace vanilla's KeyboardHandler or MouseHandler . It does not cancel other mods' key events or remap their bindings. It does not ship a benchmark claim. The repository states that no client benchmark exists, so this site publishes no FPS or latency-improvement figure. It does not support Minecraft 1.21.x in this source tree. The archived API repository is a separate, unmaintained project; see Archived API. The latency profiler measures the time between an action being stamped at capture and being drained on the game thread. That is queue-to-drain time inside the mod, not hardware latency, not frame time, and not a comparison with vanilla. Supported builds Loader Minecraft Jar --- --- --- Fabric 26.2 inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc262.jar Fabric 26.3 inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc263.jar NeoForge 26.2 inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-nf-mc262.jar Java 25 is required. Fabric builds need Loader 0.19.0 or newer and Fabric API 0.161.0 or newer; the NeoForge build needs 26.2.0.88 or newer. Install exactly one jar. Full details are in the support matrix. Where to go next Requirements — loaders, Java and version matching. Installation — get a first launch working. First session — open the settings and verify the pipeline. Architecture — how the code is organised. Limitations — every known gap, including settings that are persisted but have no runtime effect.

records.title: Requirements
records.description: The exact loader, Java and Minecraft versions InputBooster 4.1.2-alpha supports, and how to check what you have.
records.content: InputBooster 4.1.2-alpha needs Java 25, a Fabric or NeoForge client, and Minecraft 26.2 or 26.3. There is no build for any other Minecraft version in this source tree. The short version Requirement Value --- --- Java 25 Minecraft 26.2 (Fabric, NeoForge) or 26.3 (Fabric only) Loader Fabric Loader 0.19.0+ and Fabric API 0.161.0+, or NeoForge 26.2.0.88+ Side Client only Mod loader install Exactly one InputBooster jar Java 25 The mixin manifest declares compatibilityLevel: JAVA_25 , and the Fabric fabric.mod.json requires "java": ">=25" . A Java 21 runtime cannot load the mod. A launcher can be configured for one Java version and still launch the game with another. If the game refuses to start with a class-version error, the launcher is the thing to check, not the mod. To confirm which Java a launcher uses, look at the launcher's version or profile panel, or run a command in the folder that contains the launcher: Minecraft versions Only two Minecraft versions are built from this tree: Minecraft Fabric jar NeoForge jar --- --- --- 26.2 inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc262.jar inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-nf-mc262.jar 26.3 inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc263.jar — There is no NeoForge build for 26.3. The NeoForge build targets Minecraft 26.2 through the neoforge.mods.toml dependency range 26.2,26.3) . Older versions of this mod existed for Minecraft 1.21.x. That line is not part of this source tree, and the [archived API does not make 1.21 work. If you need 1.21, you need a different build from the project's release history. Fabric requirements The Fabric build declares these dependencies: "depends": { "fabricloader": ">=0.19.0", "fabric-api": ">=0.161.0", "minecraft": ">=26.3 =25" } The 26.2 jar replaces the Minecraft range with >=26.2 The 26.3 jar uses >=26.3 NeoForge requirements The NeoForge build requires neoforge 26.2.0.88,) and minecraft [26.2,26.3) . NeoForge bundles the loader, so there is no separate Fabric API requirement. The mod is declared side="CLIENT" . Checking what you have Before installing, confirm three things: The Minecraft version in your launcher matches the jar's mc262 or mc263 suffix. Your loader version is new enough for the table above. Your Java is 25. The [jar matrix page maps every published jar to its version range, and installing covers the actual file placement. What you do not need A server-side install. The mod is client only. A server does not install it, does not need a plugin for it, and cannot see it. Fabric API on NeoForge. Not applicable. A separate API mod. The public API repository is archived and is not wired into 26.x. See archived API.

records.title: Installation
records.description: Install the right InputBooster jar for your loader and Minecraft version, verify it loaded, and find the files it writes.
records.content: Installation is one jar in one folder. The only real decision is which jar: pick the one whose mc262 or mc263 suffix matches your Minecraft version and your loader. Before you start Requirements — confirm Java 25 and your loader version. Jar matrix — the full table of published jars and their version ranges. Install Match the mc262 or mc263 suffix to your Minecraft version and the loader name to your loader. Never install two InputBooster jars at once — both register the same key mappings and the same mixins, and the client will crash during class transformation. The folder is the mods directory inside your Minecraft installation. On the official launcher it is the one with the versions folder next to it. Launch Minecraft. The mod is client only, so join a world to test it; the settings button is on the options screen, not in a server list. Look for the ready line. If it is missing, the mod did not load. inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc262.jar and inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc263.jar are different builds of the same mod. Installing both puts two copies of GameTickMixin and two KeyboardHandlerMixin into the same class, which fails the client at startup. Fabric Fabric needs three things in mods : the InputBooster jar, Fabric API, and any other mods you use. NeoForge NeoForge has no separate API jar. The mod goes in the same mods folder. Verify it loaded The mod prints a ready line during initialisation. Open the log file and look for it: [InputBooster] Starting v4.1.2-alpha [Mixin] All client hooks present. [Mixin] Screen hooks: setScreenAndShow=true, setScreen=false [inputbooster-config] Loading config from .../config/inputbooster.properties [inputbooster-config] ✓ Config loaded successfully (config version 305) [Input] Polling thread started at 200 Hz. [InputBooster] Ready! If you see Ready! , the engine, the poller and the mixins are all live. The lines above it tell you which optional parts applied; the log reference explains each one. [InputBooster] Fatal init error! InputBooster is disabled for this session. means initialisation threw, the mod disabled itself, and nothing in it will work. The stack trace above that line is the actual cause. Removing the jar and re-reading the common issues page is faster than guessing. Where the mod writes Everything lives next to the game, in the config folder: The inputbooster.properties file is created on the first launch with every default in it. The two other files only appear when you use profiles. The config is written when the settings screen saves and when the client shuts down. Editing inputbooster.properties while the game is running means your edit can be overwritten at the next save. Close the game first. Removing it Delete the jar. The config files stay where they are, so a reinstall picks up your old settings. Delete config/inputbooster.properties as well if you want a clean start; the mod recreates it with defaults on the next launch. Next First session — open the settings and confirm the engine is doing what you expect. Updating — moving between versions without losing your settings. Client only — what the mod sends to a server, and what it does not.

records.title: First session
records.description: Walk through the InputBooster settings screen once, from the options button to a verified working pipeline.
records.content: Ten minutes with the settings screen will tell you more than any description. This page is a checklist: open the screen, confirm the engine is running, try one recovery case, then set the values you actually want. Open the settings Press Esc in game, or use the menu. The InputBooster button sits in the top right of the options screen. The Overview tab is live state, not settings. It tells you whether the poller is running, what rate it is using, how deep the queue is and which input mods were detected. This is where you find out whether the event hooks applied. If the event source is live, the engine is running in event-driven mode. Join a world and tap your attack key quickly. At low FPS the mod recovers taps vanilla would swallow. Changes apply as you make them. The Save Close button writes them to disk. The options button is the reliable route. The README also mentions an InputBooster category on the key-binding screen, but in the current source the two key mappings are registered under Minecraft's Misc category, so they appear there instead. See key binds. The window itself The settings window is a real window, not a fixed overlay. Drag the header to move it. Drag the bottom-right grip to resize it, down to 380x260. Scroll the content with the wheel or the scrollbar when a section is taller than the window. The tab rail and the footer stay fixed while the content scrolls. The chosen size and position are kept for the session. They are deliberately not written to the config file: they are a view preference, not a mod setting. Read the Overview tab Live The Overview tab shows values that change while you play: Row What it means --- --- Engine auto , event or poll — how the engine is currently observing input Poll thread running or stopped Rate The current sampling rate in Hz Queue Queued actions against the 128-entry bound Overlay Whether the overlay is on and where it is drawn Keys / Mouse Event counters since start Detected input mods Known input mods found on the class path The poller is a daemon thread started during initialisation. If it stopped, the mod is not sampling input. Check the log for [Input] Polling thread stopped. and see diagnosing input. Confirm the engine mode The Compatibility tab shows the resolved engine mode and the reason behind it. Situation Mode you should see --- --- No known input mod, event hooks live event No known input mod, hooks not live poll Controlify, Midnight Controls, Controllable, Sodium, Iris or Zoomify present poll You forced Event mode but the hooks never fired poll with a fallback reason The full rules are in engine modes. Try one recovery case The clearest demonstration is a tap that vanilla would miss: Open a world. Throttle your frame rate deliberately, or use a machine that cannot hold 60 FPS. Tap the attack key in short bursts. Watch the queue depth in the Overview tab while you tap. A tap that begins and ends inside one tick produces an ATTACK_PRESSED action that the drainer executes at the start of the next tick. The server sees an ordinary attack. The mod publishes no FPS or latency improvement figure, because the repository states that no client benchmark exists. The internal latency profiler measures queue-to-drain time inside the mod, which is not a comparison against vanilla. See limitations. Set the values you want A reasonable starting point for most players: Setting Value Why --- --- --- Poll rate Auto Follows the frame rate instead of a fixed number Burst mode On Pushes to 1000 Hz for three seconds after a frame-rate drop CPS limiter On, 20 Caps your click rate without changing your aim Engine mode Automatic Picks the right source for your mod set Overlay On, F3 only Visible while debugging, invisible otherwise Safe mode On Disables a feature that keeps failing, instead of the client Alpha keyboard handler Off It is alpha; enable it deliberately Every one of these is a real config key. The full list with ranges and defaults is in the configuration reference. Save and verify Close the window with Save Close. The config file is written atomically: a temporary file is created, filled and then moved into place, so a crash during the save cannot leave you with a half-written file. Then confirm the values took: poll_rate_auto=true poll_rate_hz=200 cps_limiter=true max_cps=20 engine_mode=0 safe_mode=true config_version=305 What to read next The settings screen — all seven tabs, control by control. Combat and movement — what the movement helpers actually do to your velocity. Profiles — switching settings per server. Common issues — when something does not work.

records.title: Updating
records.description: Move between InputBooster versions, keep or reset your settings, and roll back safely when a new build misbehaves.

headings.text: What is preserved across an update

records.content: Updating is a file swap. The only thing that needs care is the config schema version and the fact that a bad alpha can stop the client from starting. The update procedure Not just the world — the whole client. The mod writes its config on shutdown, and a jar swap while the game is running corrupts the next save. Remove every InputBooster jar from mods . Do not keep the old one as a backup inside the folder; the client loads every jar it finds. Exactly one jar, matching your loader and Minecraft version. See the jar matrix. The mod logs the schema version it loaded and whether it migrated anything. Open the settings screen and confirm the values survived. Schema versions The config carries a config_version . The current schema is 305 . Schema Introduced in Meaning --- --- --- 305 4.1.0-alpha Current. Adds the nine 4.1 engine and overlay keys. 303 and earlier 3.x Older schema, migrated on load. When the mod loads a file with a lower version, it logs a migration line and renames three legacy keys: Old key New key --- --- auto_sprint_key auto_sprint watap wtap_assist pollrate poll_rate_hz The migration only renames keys. Every key you did not set keeps its default, and every key that cannot be parsed is reset to its default and named in a single warning line. See validation. What is preserved across an update Your config file is read on launch and written on shutdown. A version change does not touch it unless the schema version changed. Preserved: every key present in your file, as long as it parses and stays inside its range. Reset to defaults: keys that were missing from the file, keys with an unparsable value, and keys whose value falls outside the allowed range. Not preserved: the settings window's size and position. Those are session state by design and are never written to disk. When you update from 4.0 to 4.1, the nine new keys appear with their default values. They were not in your file, so they were never yours. The configuration reference lists which key belongs to which version. Rolling back A rollback is the same procedure in reverse: delete the new jar, put the old one back. The risk is a config the new version wrote that the old version does not know. Because the loader starts from the documented defaults and only applies keys that are present in the file, an unknown key is simply ignored by the older build. Rolling back does not break the config. A jar sitting in your Downloads folder costs nothing and saves a session when 4.1.2-alpha misbehaves. Keep 4.0.3-stable there. Downgrading past the schema If you move from 4.1 back to a 3.x build, the schema version in your file will be higher than that build understands. Older builds read config_version but do not have a migration path, so they simply use the keys they recognise. Nothing crashes; the newer keys are ignored. After every update Run through this short list: Ready! appears in the log. The Overview tab shows the poll thread running. The engine mode is the one you expect. Your poll rate and CPS cap are the values you set. If the poll rate or cap came back as a default, the file was reset on load. The reason is in the log line that starts with Config entries reset to defaults . The log reference explains it.

records.title: Client only
records.description: What InputBooster sends to a server, what it cannot do, and why there is no server-side component.

headings.text: What the mod does not do
Why there is no server component

records.content: InputBooster runs entirely in your client. A server does not install it, does not detect it, and cannot see it. Every action the mod produces ends in an ordinary vanilla client call. Where it runs The mod metadata declares the client side in both loaders: "environment": "client", "entrypoints": { "client": [ "dev.inputbooster.platform.InputBoosterFabric" ] } [[dependencies.${mod_id}]] modId="minecraft" type="required" versionRange="${minecraft_version_range}" ordering="NONE" side="CLIENT" There is no server entrypoint, no network packet and no server-side mixin in the project. What the server receives The mod does not send packets of its own. It calls the same vanilla entry points a player would call: Action Vanilla call Server sees --- --- --- Attack an entity gameMode.attack(player, target) An ordinary attack packet Use item gameMode.useItem(player, InteractionHand.MAIN_HAND) An ordinary use packet Jump player.jumpFromGround() The usual movement state Sprint player.setSprinting(true) The usual movement state The server sees the same packets a vanilla client sends. It cannot distinguish a recovered tap from a tap that happened to land inside a tick. That is the design constraint, not an accident. What the mod does not do It does not extend reach. The drainer only attacks a target that is still alive and within vanilla melee range — squared distance 36, which is the 6-block reach vanilla uses. It does not change hit registration or attack cooldown. It does not generate input. Every action starts from a physical key or button press that the mod observed. It does not cancel another mod's key events or remap another mod's bindings. It does not play the game for you. There is no auto-attack loop, no auto- mine and no aim assist. Why there is no server component A server-side component would have to either: Trust the client, which changes nothing about how the client works. Validate actions, which is the server's job already for reach and cooldown. The problem the mod solves is entirely client-side: the game reads input once per tick, so a tap that starts and ends inside one tick window is never seen. No server can fix that, because the action never leaves the client. Any client mod changes what your client sends. Some servers and anticheat systems have their own rules about modified clients, and the InputBooster project does not make any claim about which servers permit it. That decision belongs to the server operator and to you. Multiplayer and other players Other players see the same thing they would see from a vanilla client: your attacks land, your movement changes, your items get used. Nothing about the mod's internal state — poll rate, queue depth, engine mode — is transmitted. The replay recorder is a local testing tool. Recordings live in memory only, are never written to disk and are never sent anywhere. Related pages Requirements — what the mod needs on your machine. Installation — putting the jar in place. Limitations — the full list of what the current build does not do.

records.title: Key binds
records.description: The two InputBooster key bindings, the Ctrl+1-5 poll rate presets, and the twelve bindings the mod tracks for you.

headings.text: The twelve bindings the mod tracks

records.content: InputBooster registers two key mappings of its own. Everything else it does starts from the twelve vanilla bindings it reads, never from a binding it creates. The mod's own bindings Key Action Config that gates it --- --- --- R Start or stop replay recording replay_enabled K Play the recording back replay_enabled Both are created in InputBoosterMod.createKeyMappings() : replayRecordKey = new KeyMapping( "key.inputbooster.replay_record", InputConstants.KEY_R, KeyMapping.Category.MISC); replayPlayKey = new KeyMapping( "key.inputbooster.replay_play", InputConstants.KEY_K, KeyMapping.Category.MISC); The README says the bindings appear in an InputBooster category. The source registers them under KeyMapping.Category.MISC , so on a vanilla client you will find them in the Misc section of the controls screen. Rebinding works normally from there. There is no "open settings" binding. The settings screen is opened from the options screen only. Combo keys With combo_keys enabled, holding Ctrl and pressing a number key applies a manual poll rate preset: Chord Poll rate --- --- Ctrl + 1 100 Hz Ctrl + 2 200 Hz Ctrl + 3 350 Hz Ctrl + 4 500 Hz Ctrl + 5 1000 Hz Applying a preset switches poll_rate_auto off and sets poll_rate_hz . The rate is confirmed with an action-bar message. The combo key handler tracks whether each digit is already held, so holding Ctrl + 1 applies the preset once, not once per tick. Opening a screen resets the latch, and releasing Ctrl resets it too. The presets live in ComboKeyPresets : public static final int[] HZ = { 100, 200, 350, 500, 1000 }; The twelve bindings the mod tracks The mod reads your actual key bindings, so if you rebind attack to a mouse button, the mod follows. The twelve it reads are: Action Vanilla binding Mod action --- --- --- Attack keyAttack ATTACK_PRESSED / ATTACK_RELEASED Use keyUse USE_PRESSED / USE_RELEASED Sprint keySprint SPRINT_PRESSED / SPRINT_RELEASED Sneak keyShift SNEAK_PRESSED / SNEAK_RELEASED Jump keyJump JUMP_PRESSED Forward keyUp FORWARD_PRESSED / FORWARD_RELEASED Back keyDown BACK_PRESSED / BACK_RELEASED Left keyLeft LEFT_PRESSED / LEFT_RELEASED Right keyRight RIGHT_PRESSED / RIGHT_RELEASED Drop keyDrop DROP_PRESSED Swap offhand keySwapOffhand SWAP_PRESSED Pick block keyPickItem PICK_BLOCK_PRESSED If a binding cannot be read, the mod substitutes the vanilla default for that slot and logs Could not read every key binding; using vanilla defaults for the rest. The Keyboard tab of the settings screen reports whether all twelve resolved. Bindings are republished every client tick, because you can rebind while the game is running. The published set is only replaced when a code actually changed, so the polling thread does not re-read an unchanged binding list on every sample. Key conflicts key_conflict_warn enables the conflict detector. It compares the mod's own bindings against the vanilla movement and action bindings and warns when they clash. A conflict is not an error. It means the same physical key is bound to two things, so one press does two things. The detector warns; it does not intercept, cancel or remap anything. Rebinding Standard vanilla behaviour: open the controls screen, find the binding, click it, press the new key. The mod's bindings are in the Misc category, alongside vanilla's other bindings. Nothing in the mod blocks or overrides a rebind — the published binding set is rebuilt from the options object every tick. Related pages The settings screen — the tab each setting lives in. records.title: Input recovery
records.description: How a tap that starts and ends between two ticks is recovered, what the mod does with it, and what it cannot recover.
records.content: A tick is 50 milliseconds long. Minecraft reads most gameplay input once per tick, so a tap that starts and ends inside that window is never seen. InputBooster samples faster than the tick and preserves the edge. The problem Vanilla's keyboard and mouse handlers tell the player what is true at the moment the tick runs. Consider a 30 ms tap on the attack key: tick ──────────────► tick ──────────────► tick │ │ └─ down ──┬── up ─┘ └─ attack happens here, if at all If the key is already released when the tick runs, the press is gone. Nothing was queued, so no attack happens. The same window swallows a jump, a use, and a sprint key. The window is wider when the frame rate is low, and it widens further during a stutter — exactly when input matters most. The recovery The mod samples the platform key state at a configurable rate, from 60 to 1000 Hz. A 30 ms tap at 200 Hz is several samples wide, so the down transition and the up transition are both observed. The result is one action per physical edge: sample ──► down seen ──► action queued ──► drained at the next tick head up seen ──► release queued ──► drained with it Two rules keep this honest: Nothing executes while a screen is open. A click in a chest is a chest click. The decision is made on the game thread, from the game's own show-screen call. Vanilla's own action is suppressed for that tick. If the mod already fired the attack, vanilla must not fire a second one for the same physical click. The state machine holds one boolean per tracked binding. A press seen by the event hook first makes the poller's later look a no-op, and the other way round. There is no timing window and no "already handled" flag that could leak between ticks. Where the recovered action goes The drainer runs at the head of the client tick and executes queued actions through vanilla's own calls: Action What runs --- --- Attack gameMode.attack(player, target) plus the swing animation Use gameMode.useItem(player, MAIN_HAND) — only when the crosshair hits nothing Jump player.jumpFromGround() when the player can leave the ground Sprint player.setSprinting(true) Sneak player.setSneaking(true) Forward release The W-tap helper runs Drop player.dropSelectedItem() Pick block The vanilla pick-block helper, only over a block Only actions in the mod's twelve tracked bindings are observed. A key that vanilla reads outside the tick loop — typing in chat, for instance — is not part of this path. And the mod never invents an action: there is no press, so there is no action. Counting The mod keeps a recoveredInputs counter, incremented every time an action is successfully queued. The Overview tab shows the session total, and the session statistics track an estimate of how many inputs would have been missed without the mod. The estimate is computed from the FPS history and the recovered count using a fixed miss-rate formula. It is an estimate, not a measurement, and it is not comparable to any other client. Treat it as a rough indicator, not a number to quote. The latency profiler LatencyProfiler measures the time between an action being stamped at capture and being drained on the game thread. It keeps a rolling 128-sample window and a session-wide peak. Queue-to-drain time inside the mod is not hardware latency, not frame time, and not a comparison with vanilla. The repository states that no client benchmark exists, so this site publishes no FPS or latency-improvement figure. The Advanced tab can reset the peak. The profiler itself is not shown on the overlay. When recovery does not happen A screen is open. The queue is cleared and the poller follows the state silently, so a key held through a pause is not reported as a fresh press when play resumes. The client is paused or there is no player. Same silent follow. The window loses focus. The engine releases every held key. The queue is full. 128 entries is the bound. Beyond it, new actions are rejected and counted as dropped, not silently discarded. The CPS limiter blocks the click. The action is dropped on purpose, and vanilla's attack is suppressed for that tick so the blocked click does not sneak through as a vanilla one. Related pages Combat and movement — the helpers built on top of recovery. Input pipeline — the code path in detail. Actions — every action and exactly what it does.

records.title: Combat and movement
records.description: What sprint fix, W-tap, anti-idle, auto-strafe, the CPS limiter and burst mode actually do, with their exact conditions.
records.content: These helpers are small, conditional and easy to misread. Each one has a precondition, and most of them do nothing unless that precondition holds. This page lists the conditions exactly as the code has them. Movement helpers Sprint fix and auto-sprint SprintManager runs only when sprint_fix is enabled. It has two halves: Auto-sprint ( auto_sprint ): sets player.setSprinting(true) whenever forward is held, the player is not sneaking, and food level is above 6. It returns early, so the manual sprint key is not consulted in that case. Manual sprint : if the sprint key is held together with forward, and the player is not sneaking, and food level is above 6, the player is set to sprinting. Condition Effect --- --- Forward held, not sneaking, food > 6 Sprinting Food at 6 or below No sprint Sneaking No sprint auto_sprint is checked inside SprintManager , and the whole manager is skipped when sprint_fix is off. Turning off sprint fix turns off auto-sprint too, whatever the auto_sprint value says. W-tap assist WTapAssist acts on the tick after forward is released: Vec3 vel = player.getDeltaMovement(); player.setDeltaMovement(vel.x 0.6, vel.y, vel.z 0.6); Horizontal velocity is multiplied by 0.6 on the tick following the release of forward. The velocity is only touched when forward is genuinely up. This is a local velocity change. It does not send extra packets, and it does not change what the server validates. Anti-idle AntiIdleManager adds 0.0001 degrees to the player's yaw every 200 ticks — roughly every ten seconds. That is far below the threshold at which the server would consider the player to be turning. It exists to keep a session from being treated as idle. It is not an anti-AFK that plays for you. Auto-strafe AutoStrafeManager applies a yaw nudge, and every one of these must hold: Condition Value --- --- auto_strafe enabled yes The player is sprinting required FPS 40 or lower Forward is held required Exactly one strafe key is held left xor right The applied delta is ±0.4 (40 / FPS) degrees. At 20 FPS that is 0.8 degrees per tick; at 40 FPS it is 0.4. Above 40 FPS the game is fast enough that vanilla movement already looks smooth, and the correction would be visible. The mod only applies it when the frame rate is low enough to need help. The CPS limiter CpsLimiter caps how many attacks per second reach the game. It is a token bucket: the bucket refills at max_cps tokens per second and holds at most max_cps tokens, so the long-run average is capped while short bursts pass through. The bucket starts full, so your first burst after joining a world is not swallowed. The four modes The effective cap is computed once per second and reused for that whole second, so two clicks in the same second always see the same limit. Mode Effective cap --- --- FIXED max_cps HUMANIZED max_cps minus a deterministic jitter of 0 to 2 WEAPON_AWARE min(max_cps, 16) COOLDOWN min(max_cps, 18) , plus a minimum gap between accepted clicks COOLDOWN additionally requires a gap of max(35 ms, 1000 / max_cps) between two accepted clicks. The gap is computed in milliseconds first and converted to nanoseconds once. cps_mode is read, upper-cased and stored, but it is never checked against the four known names. An unknown value falls through to the FIXED branch of the switch, because that is the default arm. What a blocked click does When the limiter rejects an attack, the mod still suppresses vanilla's attack for that tick. A blocked click stays blocked; it does not leak through as a vanilla click. Modes and the max_cps slider max_cps ranges from 1 to 20. WEAPON_AWARE and COOLDOWN can only lower it, never raise it. Burst mode With burst_mode enabled, the mod watches the frame rate. When it drops by more than 20 percent in one tick — and the previous frame rate was above 10 — the poller runs at 1000 Hz for 60 ticks, about three seconds. FPS dropped from 120 to 80 (33%), bursting to 1000 Hz for 3s The action bar confirms the burst and its end when show_action_bar is on. While bursting, the polling thread samples at 1000 Hz regardless of poll_rate_hz and regardless of whether automatic mode is on. The Overview tab shows 1000 while a burst is active. Click sounds click_sounds is off by default. When it is on, a click sound plays for actions the mod executed — but only for physical input, never for a replayed event. Setting Range Default --- --- --- click_sound_pitch 0.5 to 2.0 1.35 click_sound_volume 0.0 to 1.0 0.35 Safe mode If a feature throws repeatedly, safe mode disables that feature instead of letting it take the client down. Five errors within ten seconds for one module disables that module; it is re-enabled after a quiet window. The modules safe mode knows about are input , combat , movement , debug , profiles , anti_idle and replay . The input module is the execution layer itself, so safe mode can stop the mod from touching the player while the rest of the mod keeps running. The log line Safe Mode disabled module 'x' after repeated errors names the module. A feature that stops working after a crash elsewhere in the session is usually safe mode, not a bug in the feature. Related pages Input recovery — the core mechanic these helpers build on. The overlay — watching the rate and counters live. Feature managers — the code behind these helpers.

records.title: The overlay
records.description: What the InputBooster HUD overlay draws, the exact conditions under which it appears, and how to configure it.
records.content: The overlay is a small panel drawn over the HUD. It shows the engine state, the event counters and the dispatch timing. It is off by default outside the F3 debug screen. When it draws All of these must be true: Condition Source --- --- show_f3_info is on The master switch A player exists mc.player != null overlay_opacity is above 0.001 opacity > 0.001f overlay_mode is 1, or the F3 debug screen is open overlay_mode The vanilla HUD Overlay option in the options screen must also be enabled, otherwise the game does not draw the HUD at all. overlay_mode is 0 by default, which means the overlay only appears while the F3 debug screen is open. Set it to 1 to keep it on during normal play. What it shows Line Config that toggles it Content --- --- --- Title always InputBooster Engine overlay_show_engine The engine mode and the current rate in Hz Counters overlay_show_events Keys, mouse and actions, abbreviated above 1000 Dispatch overlay_show_overhead Mean dispatch cost in microseconds and the queue depth Warning always, when relevant Custom keyboard handler is ALPHA A rendered panel looks like this: InputBooster 4.1.2-alpha Engine: poll 200 Hz Keys 1.2k Mouse 430 Actions 880 Dispatch 3.41 us Queue 0/128 The counter line abbreviates: 1.2k for 1200, 4.5m for 4,500,000. The overlay shows dispatch timing, not input latency. LatencyProfiler keeps a rolling average and a peak, but those are not part of the overlay's line list — the peak is shown on the settings screen instead. Queue-to-drain time is also not a latency comparison against vanilla. Placement overlay_position selects one of four corners: Value Corner --- --- 0 Top-left (default) 1 Top-right 2 Bottom-left 3 Bottom-right The position is clamped inside the window, so the panel is never drawn off screen after a resize. A panel larger than the screen is pinned to 0 rather than drawn at a negative coordinate. int maxX = Math.max(0, screenWidth - panelWidth); int maxY = Math.max(0, screenHeight - panelHeight); return new Pos(clamp(x, maxX), clamp(y, maxY)); Scale and opacity Setting Range Default Effect --- --- --- --- overlay_scale 0.5 to 3.0 1.0 Multiplies the panel size and the glyphs together overlay_opacity 0.0 to 1.0 0.8 The alpha of the panel background Opacity multiplies the panel background, not the text. The text colours are full-alpha ARGB values. The earlier implementation passed 0x55FFFF and 0xFFAA00 as glyph colours. Those are RGB values with an alpha byte of zero, and the GUI treats a zero alpha as "do not draw". The panel drew and every line in it was transparent. The colours are now ARGB with 0xFF alpha. Cost The overlay's text is rebuilt at most four times a second — a 250 ms interval — and the result is kept in a reused array. The per-frame cost is one render-state submission per line, not string formatting every frame. The keystrokes overlay show_keystrokes exists as a config key, a settings toggle and a profile field. There is no renderer for it in 4.1.2-alpha, so no keystroke display appears anywhere. The toggle changes show_keystrokes in the config file and nothing else. The key is persisted and validated, which is why it looks like a working feature. See limitations for the full list of settings that are stored but have no runtime effect. The alpha handler warning When custom_keyboard_handler is on, the overlay adds a warning line. It is the only line that uses the warn colour, and it is prefixed with ! internally to select that colour. Related pages The settings screen — the Overlay tab. Diagnostics — reading the counters when something is wrong. Limitations — inert settings.

records.title: Profiles
records.description: Save a set of InputBooster settings, switch between them, and bind one to a server.

headings.text: Switching profiles and the running engine

records.content: A profile is a snapshot of 23 settings under a name. Up to five can exist at once, and one of them can be bound to a server so it loads automatically when you connect. Opening the profile screen The Advanced tab of the settings screen has a Manage profiles button. It opens a separate screen with a Save button per profile, a Load button and a Delete button per profile, and a Back button. What a profile captures A profile is a snapshot of the current configuration. It holds 23 fields: Group Fields --- --- Polling pollRateHz , pollRateAutoMode Movement sprintFixEnabled , autoSprintEnabled , wTapAssistEnabled , antiIdleEnabled , autoStrafeEnabled Combat cpsLimiterEnabled , maxCps , cpsMode Overlay showF3Info , showKeystrokes , showActionBar Diagnostics fpsCheckInterval , debugMode Engine burstModeEnabled , comboKeysEnabled Features replayEnabled , safeModeEnabled , eventLogEnabled , keyConflictWarn , perServerProfiles Overlay position, scale and opacity, the engine mode, the custom keyboard handler, the compatibility fallback, the click dedupe and scroll debounce windows, and the click sound settings are not in a profile. Applying a profile leaves those at whatever they were. Saving, loading and deleting Save captures the current settings under a name. Saving over an existing name overwrites that profile instead of creating a second one — the match is case-insensitive. Load applies the profile to the live configuration and writes the config file. An action-bar message confirms it. Delete removes a profile. If the deleted profile was the active one, nothing is active afterwards. The limit The profile list holds a maximum of five profiles. Saving a sixth with a new name fails and the list stays at five. Where profiles are stored Profiles live in a JSON array next to the config file: The file is written atomically, like the main config. A profile file that is not valid JSON is moved aside to inputbooster_profiles.json.corrupt and the game starts with no profiles instead of failing to launch. Per-server profiles With per_server_profiles enabled, the mod watches which server you are connected to and loads the profile bound to it. Detection runs every 20 ticks, roughly once a second, and uses reflection with a defensive fallback — the vanilla fields it looks up have changed across versions, so a failure degrades to a stable identifier instead of throwing on the client tick. The identifier is normalised so the same server always maps to the same profile: Address Normalised to --- --- Example.com example.com example.com:25565 example.com tcp://EXAMPLE.COM example.com example.com/somepath example.com — (singleplayer) singleplayer — (main menu) title Writing a binding PerServerProfileManager.bind() exists and writes the file correctly, but no button in the settings screen calls it. The binding file has to be edited by hand while the game is closed. Create or edit inputbooster_server_profiles.properties : example.com=Competitive hypixel.net=Slow singleplayer=Casual The key is the normalised server identifier and the value is the profile name. The name must match a profile exactly as it appears in the profiles list, otherwise the lookup finds nothing and your settings simply do not change. The manager normalises the identifier it detects, but it normalises the file key when it saves. When you edit the file by hand, write the normalised form: lower case, no scheme, no path, no :25565 . Switching profiles and the running engine Applying a profile changes the live configuration. Two settings have an immediate effect on the running poller: Setting Effect on apply --- --- pollRateHz , pollRateAutoMode The poller's rate is updated on the next tick engineMode Not part of a profile — see the note below engine_mode is not one of the 23 captured fields. If you switch profiles, the engine mode stays whatever it was. Related pages The configuration file — the main properties file. Profile file format — the JSON schema, field by field. Per-server profiles — the binding file format.

records.title: Replay and logs
records.description: The R and K replay bindings, what a recording contains, and how the in-memory event log works.

headings.text: It never runs behind a screen
A full queue pauses, it does not skip

records.content: Replay is a testing tool, not a macro. It records the actions the mod queued and plays them back, so you can check that a sequence of inputs behaves the same when it is not you pressing the keys. Using it Key Action --- --- R Start or stop recording K Play the recording back The current state is shown with an action-bar message when you toggle recording: InputBooster replay REC InputBooster replay STOP Playback does nothing when there is no recording. The log says [Replay] Nothing recorded yet. What a recording contains A recording stores the actions the mod queued , not raw hardware presses and not events the drainer later rejected. A replay therefore reproduces exactly what the mod itself would have executed. Each frame is an action plus the offset in nanoseconds from the start of the recording. Playback replays the offsets, so the timing of the original sequence is preserved. The rules It never fights you While physical input is waiting in the queue, playback holds back and rewinds its clock slightly so it stays in sync. A recording can never be injected on top of a live click. if (InputActionQueue.pendingPhysical() > 0) { playStart += elapsed / 100; // rewind slightly to stay in sync return; } It never runs behind a screen Playback only advances when the player owns the keyboard. Opening a chest pauses it. Without this, the drainer would clear the queue behind the screen and the recording would silently lose events. It never double-fires Replayed events are tagged with Origin.REPLAY . A replayed attack does not tick the hit counter, does not add to the CPS graph and does not play the click sound. A full queue pauses, it does not skip If the queue is full when playback tries to submit an event, the index is not advanced. The event is retried on the next tick. After 20 consecutive stalled ticks — about a second — that one event is dropped and counted. Limits Property Value --- --- Maximum events 4000 Storage In memory only, never written to disk Lifetime Ends with the session Truncation Recorded events past the limit are counted, not stored If a recording hits the limit, stopping it logs: [Replay] Recording stopped early: buffer full, 12 event(s) not stored. 4000 events at a normal click rate is a long recording. The bound exists so a long session cannot grow the buffer without limit. The event log EventLog is a bounded in-memory list of the last 80 events, each stamped with the wall-clock time to the second. Property Value --- --- Maximum entries 80 Storage In memory, never written to disk Master switch event_log Events it records include: 12:41:03 InputBooster initialized 12:41:07 Attack queued 12:41:07 Entity attack fired 12:41:11 Error in input: NullPointerException 12:41:11 Safe Mode disabled module 'input' after repeated errors The log is written and it is bounded and it is correct, but in 4.1.2-alpha there is no viewer . The Advanced tab has a toggle for it, and the Compatibility tab can write a compatibility status line into it, but nothing renders the list. The only ways to see it are the internal snapshot() and latest() accessors. Session statistics The Overview tab shows a 60-second CPS graph built from one-second buckets. The session statistics track: Value Source --- --- Session start time Wall clock at construction Uptime Monotonic clock Recovered inputs The recoveredInputs counter Estimated missed inputs A heuristic from the FPS history Poller alive Whether the polling thread is running CPS history 60 one-second buckets It is computed from the recovered count and the current frame rate using a fixed miss-rate formula. It is an estimate, it is not a measurement, and it is not comparable to another client's number. Related pages Key binds — the R and K bindings and the Ctrl+1-5 presets. Troubleshooting — what to do when replay does nothing. Feature managers — the replay and log code.

records.title: The config file
records.description: Where inputbooster.properties lives, how it is written, how it is read, and what happens to a value it cannot parse.
records.content: Everything the mod remembers between sessions lives in one properties file. It is written atomically, read defensively and never fatal: a broken value costs you that one setting, not the game. Location The directory is resolved from the inputbooster.configDir system property when it is set, and config relative to the game directory otherwise. The system property exists so the automated tests can use a throwaway folder. File Purpose --- --- inputbooster.properties The main settings inputbooster_profiles.json Saved profiles, JSON inputbooster_server_profiles.properties Server-to-profile bindings The file is written when the settings screen saves and again when the client shuts down. An edit made while the game is running can be overwritten at the next save. Format A standard Java properties file: key=value , one per line, # starts a comment. #InputBooster 4.1.2-alpha configuration - by Ahaduzzaman Khan poll_rate_hz=200 poll_rate_auto=true burst_mode=true combo_keys=true sprint_fix=true auto_sprint=true wtap_assist=true anti_idle=true auto_strafe=true cps_limiter=true max_cps=20 cps_mode=FIXED click_sounds=false click_sound_pitch=1.35 click_sound_volume=0.35 replay_enabled=true safe_mode=true event_log=true key_conflict_warn=true per_server_profiles=true custom_keyboard_handler=false show_f3_info=true show_keystrokes=true overlay_position=0 overlay_scale=1.0 overlay_opacity=0.8 show_action_bar=true fps_check_interval=20 debug_mode=false engine_mode=0 keyboard_repeat_guard=true mouse_scroll_debounce_ms=0 mouse_click_dedupe_ms=0 compat_fallback=true overlay_mode=0 overlay_show_engine=true overlay_show_events=true overlay_show_overhead=true config_version=305 That is all 39 persisted keys with their default values. The full table with ranges and readers is in the key reference. How it is written The save is synchronous and atomic: The parent directory is created if it does not exist. A temporary file is created in the same directory. Every key is written to it. The temporary file is moved over the real file, atomically where the filesystem supports it. Path temp = Files.createTempFile(parent, "inputbooster", ".tmp"); try (OutputStream out = Files.newOutputStream(temp)) { props.store(out, "InputBooster " + MOD_VERSION + " configuration - by Ahaduzzaman Khan"); } try { Files.move(temp, CONFIG_PATH, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING, StandardCopyOption.ATOMIC_MOVE); } catch (AtomicMoveNotSupportedException e) { Files.move(temp, CONFIG_PATH, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING); } The UI thread, the game thread and the shutdown path can all save. Before the temp-file approach, a save that raced with another one left a truncated file and wiped the user's settings. The move is atomic, so a reader sees either the old file or the new one, never a half-written one. How it is read load() starts from the documented defaults every time and then applies the file. That ordering matters: an earlier version only assigned the keys that were present, so any key missing from the file kept whatever value it had in memory — importing a partial config leaked the previous session's settings. Accepted boolean spellings Spelling Result --- --- true , True , TRUE true yes , Yes true 1 true on , On true false , False false no , No false 0 false off , Off false Boolean.parseBoolean only accepts a lowercase true , so True , yes and 1 all resolved to false. Hand-edited configs silently disabled features, which is why the parser accepts the common spellings. Anything else falls back to the default, and the key is named in the warning line described in validation. Ranges Numeric values are clamped, not rejected, when they are read and when they are set: Key Range --- --- poll_rate_hz 60 to 1000 max_cps 1 to 20 click_sound_pitch 0.5 to 2.0 click_sound_volume 0.0 to 1.0 overlay_position 0 to 3 overlay_scale 0.5 to 3.0 overlay_opacity 0.0 to 1.0 fps_check_interval 1 to 100 engine_mode 0 to 2 mouse_scroll_debounce_ms 0 to 200 mouse_click_dedupe_ms 0 to 100 overlay_mode 0 to 1 The schema version config_version is the on-disk schema version. The current value is 305 . When the mod loads a file with a lower version it logs a migration line and renames three legacy keys: Legacy key Current key --- --- auto_sprint_key auto_sprint watap wtap_assist pollrate poll_rate_hz The version is written back on the next save, so a migrated file stops migrating. The three files Only the first is created automatically. The profile file appears when you save a profile; the bindings file appears when a binding is written. Related pages Key reference — every key, its default, its range and what reads it. Validation — what happens to a bad value. Profile format — the JSON schema.

records.title: Key reference
records.description: All 39 persisted configuration keys with their default, their allowed range and the code that reads them.
records.content: Every key InputBooster writes, what it does, and — for four of them — the fact that nothing reads them yet. Polling Key Default Range Read by Effect --- --- --- --- --- poll_rate_auto true boolean InputBoosterMod.onClientTick Follows the frame rate instead of a fixed rate poll_rate_hz 200 60–1000 InputPollingThread , adjustPollRateManual The fixed sampling rate burst_mode true boolean BurstModeManager 1000 Hz for three seconds after a frame-rate drop combo_keys true boolean InputBoosterMod.handleComboKeys The Ctrl+1-5 poll rate presets fps_check_interval 20 1–100 — No effect. The adaptive rate is recomputed every tick regardless Movement and combat Key Default Range Read by Effect --- --- --- --- --- sprint_fix true boolean SprintManager , ModuleManager Enables the whole sprint manager auto_sprint true boolean SprintManager Sprint while moving forward wtap_assist true boolean WTapAssist Horizontal velocity multiplied by 0.6 after W is released anti_idle true boolean AntiIdleManager A tiny yaw nudge every 200 ticks auto_strafe true boolean AutoStrafeManager Low-FPS strafe correction below 40 FPS cps_limiter true boolean CpsLimiter , ModuleManager Enables the click rate cap max_cps 20 1–20 CpsLimiter The cap the limiter enforces cps_mode FIXED string CpsLimiter FIXED , HUMANIZED , WEAPON_AWARE or COOLDOWN The value is upper-cased and stored, but it is never checked against the four known names. An unknown value falls through to the FIXED branch of the switch, because that is the default arm. Mouse Key Default Range Read by Effect --- --- --- --- --- mouse_click_dedupe_ms 0 0–100 InputEngine.clickDedupeMs , InputEventDispatcher Minimum gap between two accepted attacks mouse_scroll_debounce_ms 0 0–200 MouseProcessor.onScroll Ignores repeat wheel events inside the window click_sounds false boolean InputClickSoundManager Plays a UI click for executed actions click_sound_pitch 1.35 0.5–2.0 InputClickSoundManager The pitch of that sound click_sound_volume 0.35 0.0–1.0 — No audible effect. The sound instance is created with the pitch only Scrolling is only counted by the mod. It never applies scroll input to the game. The click sound plays for every pressed action the mod executed — attack, use, sprint, sneak, jump, the four movement keys, drop, swap and pick block — with a minimum interval of 18 ms between sounds. Replayed events do not play it. InputClickSoundManager builds the sound with SimpleSoundInstance.forUI(sound, pitch) . The configured volume is never passed to it, so changing click_sound_volume changes the file and the slider but not the sound you hear. Engine Key Default Range Read by Effect --- --- --- --- --- engine_mode 0 0–2 CompatibilityManager.resolveMode 0 automatic, 1 event driven, 2 polled keyboard_repeat_guard true boolean — No effect. A repeat action is ignored unconditionally compat_fallback true boolean CompatibilityManager.resolveMode Poll instead of competing with a detected input mod custom_keyboard_handler false boolean KeyboardRouter , InputPollingThread The alpha keyboard handler KeyboardProcessor ignores GLFW's REPEAT action unconditionally, before the guard is consulted. The behaviour you get is "a held key is one press" whatever the toggle says — the toggle is simply not in the path. It does not gate the replay status messages, the profile-loaded message or the combo key rate message; those are sent unconditionally.
