records.title: Validation
records.description: Exactly what the mod does with a value it cannot parse, which keys are checked, and which are silently reset.

headings.text: What a broken file cannot do

records.content: A broken config value costs you that one setting and nothing else. This page lists which keys are checked, which are not, and what the log says when something is reset. The load order Every field is set back to its default before the file is read. Nothing survives from the previous session unless the file says so. The file is parsed as a Java properties file. A file that does not exist causes the defaults to be written out instead. If the schema version is older than 305, three legacy keys are renamed and the version is updated. Each key is parsed and clamped into its allowed range. Keys that could not be used are collected and named in one warning line. Booleans Seven spellings are accepted, in any case: true , yes , 1 , on are true. false , no , 0 , off are false. Anything else falls back to the default. The comparison trims surrounding whitespace first, so true is valid. Numbers An integer that cannot be parsed falls back to the default. A parsed value outside the allowed range is clamped: Key Below range Above range --- --- --- poll_rate_hz 60 1000 max_cps 1 20 overlay_position 0 3 fps_check_interval 1 100 engine_mode 0 2 mouse_scroll_debounce_ms 0 200 mouse_click_dedupe_ms 0 100 overlay_mode 0 1 overlay_scale 0.5 3.0 overlay_opacity 0.0 1.0 click_sound_pitch 0.5 2.0 click_sound_volume 0.0 1.0 The same clamping happens when a value is set through the settings screen, so a value in the file and a value in the UI cannot produce different runtime states. The warning line Config entries reset to defaults (invalid or unparsable): poll_rate_hz=2000, combo_keys=maybe A boolean is listed by name. A number is listed as key=value so you can see what was actually in the file. The report is a single warning listing every key that had to be reset. It is logged once per load, right before the "config loaded successfully" line. Which keys are checked These keys are validated and reported when they are bad: Booleans: poll_rate_auto , sprint_fix , auto_sprint , wtap_assist , anti_idle , auto_strafe , cps_limiter , burst_mode , combo_keys , custom_keyboard_handler , keyboard_repeat_guard , compat_fallback , overlay_show_engine , overlay_show_events , overlay_show_overhead . Numbers: engine_mode , mouse_scroll_debounce_ms , mouse_click_dedupe_ms , overlay_mode , poll_rate_hz , max_cps , overlay_position , fps_check_interval . Being validated does not mean a key affects anything. Four of the checked booleans — keyboard_repeat_guard , and the three others listed under inert keys — are read nowhere that would change behaviour. Which keys are not checked These are not in the validation list. A bad value in one of them still falls back to the default, but it is not named in the warning line: click_sounds , click_sound_pitch , click_sound_volume , replay_enabled , safe_mode , event_log , key_conflict_warn , per_server_profiles , show_f3_info , show_keystrokes , show_action_bar , debug_mode , cps_mode , config_version . The validation list was written to cover the keys whose failure would be surprising. The remaining keys are either booleans that behave identically when defaulted, or values that are clamped at read time anyway. Strings cps_mode is upper-cased with Locale.ROOT and stored. It is never checked against the four known names, so a typo produces a value that behaves like FIXED — the default arm of the switch — while the file says something else. Migration Older schemas are migrated in place. The migration renames three keys: Legacy key Current key --- --- auto_sprint_key auto_sprint watap wtap_assist pollrate poll_rate_hz A rename only happens when the current key is absent, so a file that already has the new key keeps its own value. Schema versions 1 to 303 used the same key names and had no upgrade path. The current migration does not invent values or change semantics — it only renames the three keys that were spelled differently in very old builds. What a broken file cannot do Situation Result --- --- The file does not exist Defaults are written out The file is not readable A warning is logged and the defaults are used A value is unparsable That key is reset, the rest of the file is applied A value is out of range It is clamped into range A key is missing The default is used for it There is no state in which a bad config file prevents the game from starting. Related pages The config file — format and location. Key reference — every key and what reads it. Log reference — the log lines this page mentions.

records.title: Profile format
records.description: The JSON schema of inputbooster_profiles.json, every field it holds, and the per-server binding file format.

headings.text: What is not in a profile

records.content: A profile is one JSON object in an array. The format is stable enough to edit by hand, and a file that is not valid JSON is moved aside instead of breaking the game. The profile file It is a JSON array. Each element is one profile: [ { "name": "Competitive", "pollRateHz": 500, "pollRateAutoMode": false, "sprintFixEnabled": true, "autoSprintEnabled": true, "wTapAssistEnabled": true, "antiIdleEnabled": true, "autoStrafeEnabled": false, "cpsLimiterEnabled": true, "showF3Info": true, "showKeystrokes": true, "showActionBar": true, "burstModeEnabled": true, "maxCps": 20, "comboKeysEnabled": true, "fpsCheckInterval": 20, "debugMode": false, "cpsMode": "HUMANIZED", "replayEnabled": true, "safeModeEnabled": true, "eventLogEnabled": true, "keyConflictWarn": true, "perServerProfiles": true } ] Field reference All 23 fields, with the type and the default used when the field is missing. Field Type Default Notes --- --- --- --- name string Unnamed A blank name becomes Unnamed pollRateHz number 200 Clamped to 60–1000 on apply pollRateAutoMode boolean true sprintFixEnabled boolean true autoSprintEnabled boolean true wTapAssistEnabled boolean true antiIdleEnabled boolean true autoStrafeEnabled boolean true cpsLimiterEnabled boolean true showF3Info boolean true showKeystrokes boolean true Stored, but the keystroke overlay has no renderer showActionBar boolean true burstModeEnabled boolean true maxCps number 20 Clamped to 1–20 on apply comboKeysEnabled boolean true fpsCheckInterval number 20 Stored, but the adaptive rate ignores it debugMode boolean false Stored, but no logging is gated on it cpsMode string FIXED Upper-cased on apply; a blank value becomes FIXED replayEnabled boolean true safeModeEnabled boolean true eventLogEnabled boolean true keyConflictWarn boolean true perServerProfiles boolean true Every field is optional when the file is read. A missing field, a null value or a value of the wrong type falls back to that field's default. A profile written by an older version still loads. What is not in a profile These config keys are deliberately outside the profile schema: overlay_position , overlay_scale , overlay_opacity , overlay_mode , overlay_show_engine , overlay_show_events , overlay_show_overhead , engine_mode , custom_keyboard_handler , compat_fallback , keyboard_repeat_guard , mouse_scroll_debounce_ms , mouse_click_dedupe_ms , click_sounds , click_sound_pitch , click_sound_volume , config_version . Applying a profile leaves them exactly as they were. Limits and failure handling Rule Behaviour --- --- Maximum profiles 5 Reading At most the first 5 valid objects are loaded Write Atomic — a temporary file is written and then moved into place Invalid JSON The file is moved to inputbooster_profiles.json.corrupt and the game starts with no profiles Not an array Same treatment, with the reason not a JSON array Unreadable file A warning is logged; the game continues It is moved aside, not removed, so you can inspect it and repair it. The log line names the backup file and the reason. Per-server bindings A standard properties file. The key is the normalised server identifier and the value is the profile name: example.com=Competitive hypixel.net=Slow singleplayer=Casual The identifier The identifier is normalised before it is used as a key: Raw address Key --- --- Example.com example.com example.com:25565 example.com tcp://EXAMPLE.COM example.com ws://example.com example.com example.com/some/path example.com No server, singleplayer singleplayer No server, main menu title Detection failed unknown Write the normalised form when you edit the file by hand. The profile name The value is matched against the profile names exactly , ignoring case. A name that does not exist is ignored: the log records nothing and your settings simply do not change. The manager can write a binding, but no button calls it in 4.1.2-alpha. The file has to be created by hand while the game is closed. See profiles. Detection The server is detected once every 20 ticks, roughly once a second, using reflection over the vanilla server entry. The reflective lookups are individually guarded: a field that moved between Minecraft versions degrades to a stable identifier instead of throwing on the client tick. Related pages Profiles — using the profile screen. The config file — the main properties file. Key reference — the config keys a profile does and does not capture.

records.title: Architecture
records.description: How the InputBooster source tree is organised, from the loader entrypoints down to the drainer.
records.content: The mod is a loader-neutral core with two thin platform entrypoints and one version-compat shim per Minecraft version. Everything else is shared. The shape of the tree The layers E[InputEngine] K[KeyboardHandlerMixin] --> KP[KeyboardProcessor] --> E M[MouseHandlerMixin] --> MP[MouseProcessor] --> E E --> D[InputEventDispatcher] --> Q[InputActionQueue] Q --> DR[InputDrainer] --> V[Vanilla client calls] E --> C[CompatibilityManager] S[ScreenTrackingMixin] --> R[KeyboardRouter] --> DR CF[InputBoosterConfig] -.reads.-> E CF -.reads.-> DR CF -.reads.-> F[feature managers] } caption="The core path. The poller and the event mixins are the two sources; the drainer is the only place that touches the player." /> The layers in detail Platform entrypoints Two files, each a few dozen lines: File Loader What it does --- --- --- InputBoosterNeoForge.java NeoForge Calls bootstrap() , registers the key mappings, forwards the client tick InputBoosterFabric.java Fabric The same, through the Fabric client entrypoint Neither contains input logic. The core is loader-neutral: public static KeyMapping[] createKeyMappings() { ... } public static void bootstrap() { ... } public static void initialize() { ... } public static void onClientTick() { ... } public static void shutdown() { ... } On NeoForge the client-setup callback runs after the key-mapping registration event, so a registration handler only ever saw null and the bindings were silently dropped from the controls screen. The mappings are therefore created during mod construction, before the platform registers them. The engine package dev.inputbooster.engine is the input core: Class Responsibility --- --- InputEngine The state machine and the mode switch KeyStateManager The authoritative held/released state per slot KeyBindingProcessor Maps key codes to action slots KeyboardProcessor Turns a key event into an engine state change MouseProcessor Turns a button or scroll event into an engine state change InputEventDispatcher The single exit point that queues an action CompatibilityManager Detects input mods and resolves the engine mode DiagnosticsManager The counters the overlay and settings screen read ConfigurationManager A thin façade over the config accessors The input package dev.inputbooster.input holds the three pieces that answer "who owns the keyboard right now": Class Responsibility --- --- KeyboardRouter Tracks whether a screen is open KeyBindingSet The twelve bound key codes, published per tick RawKeyState A handle to the window for raw platform key state The feature package dev.inputbooster.feature holds one class per feature. Every one of them is ticked from InputBoosterMod.onClientTick() and gated by a config flag and by the module manager. See feature managers. The mixin package Ten mixins, all client side. Two observe input, one drains the queue, the rest attach the UI. See the mixin inventory. The version shim dev.inputbooster.compat.McVersion exists once per Minecraft version, in src/compat/mc26_2 and src/compat/mc26_3 . The build includes exactly one of them. It hides the differences between 26.2 and 26.3 that the mod actually touches: Difference Shim method --- --- The swing call changed shape McVersion.swingArm(player) InputConstants.isKeyDown takes a window handle in 26.2 but not in 26.3 McVersion.isKeyDown(key) Sneak and jump state access McCompat.setSneaking , McCompat.isInWater , McCompat.isClimbing Everything version-specific goes through the shim. That is why a 26.2 and a 26.3 jar share one core source tree and one engine. Threading model Thread What it touches --- --- Game thread Everything Minecraft, the drainer, the tick handlers Polling thread Raw key state and the published binding set only The polling thread never touches a Minecraft object. The window handle and the binding set are captured on the game thread and published as volatile fields. An aggressively prioritised poller starves the render thread on low-end CPUs, which is exactly the stutter the mod exists to prevent. The lifecycle bootstrap() creates the key mappings. Nothing else happens yet. onClientTick() calls initialize() , which verifies the mixin targets, loads the config, creates every manager, detects input mods, starts the poller and logs Ready! . Each tick: publish bindings, update the poll rate, run the combo keys, tick the feature managers, tick the drainer via the mixin. The close mixin calls shutdown() , which stops the poller and waits for it, clears the queue, saves the config and releases the keyboard. If initialize() throws, the mod sets initFailed , disables itself and logs Fatal init error! . It does not retry on the next tick: an earlier version logged the same stack trace every tick and could start a second polling thread per attempt. Related pages Input pipeline — the path of one action. Engine modes — how the source is chosen. Mixin inventory — every hook and its contract.

records.title: Input pipeline
records.description: The full path of one input action: capture, edge detection, dispatch, queue, drain and suppression.
records.content: One physical press becomes at most one action, queued once, drained once, and suppressed once. This page follows that path through the code. The whole path poll thread B[InputEngine.pollRaw] C[KeyboardHandlerMixin] --> HEAD, no cancel D[KeyboardProcessor] E[MouseHandlerMixin] --> HEAD, no cancel F[MouseProcessor] D --> G[InputEngine.onKeyState] F --> G B --> H[KeyStateManager.updateSlot] G --> H H --> changed I[InputEventDispatcher.submit] I --> J[InputActionQueue 128] J --> tick HEAD K[InputDrainer.drainAll] K --> L[Vanilla client call] K --> M[markAttackHandled / markUseHandled] M --> once per tick N[startAttack / startUseItem suppressed] } caption="Two sources, one state machine, one queue, one drain point." /> Stage 1 — capture The poller InputPollingThread is a daemon thread. It samples, hands the sample to the engine, and parks for the remainder of the interval: long targetNs = 1_000_000_000L / hz; long elapsed = System.nanoTime() - loopStart; long sleepNs = targetNs - elapsed; while (sleepNs > 0 && running.get()) { LockSupport.parkNanos(sleepNs); sleepNs = targetNs - (System.nanoTime() - loopStart); } LockSupport.parkNanos keeps sub-millisecond resolution. Thread.sleep is millisecond-quantised on many platforms and drifts badly at high rates. Drift is absorbed by never sleeping when the loop is already behind. The poller is gated. When the game is paused, there is no player, a screen is open or the mod is shutting down, it follows the state silently : if (gated) { engine.syncOnlyRaw(raw, bindings); // no edges emitted return; } That is why a key held through a pause is not reported as a fresh press when play resumes. The event hooks KeyboardHandlerMixin and MouseHandlerMixin observe at HEAD and cancel nothing: @Inject(method = "keyPress", at = @At("HEAD"), require = 0) private void onKeyPressObserved(long window, int action, KeyEvent event, CallbackInfo ci) { KeyboardProcessor.onKeyEvent(event.key(), action); } Vanilla still routes the event to the open screen, to the key bindings and to every other mod exactly as before. Stage 2 — edge detection Both sources write through one method: public boolean updateSlot(int slot, boolean down) { if (slot = SLOTS) return false; if (slotDown[slot] == down) return false; slotDown[slot] = down; slotChangeNanos[slot] = System.nanoTime(); return true; } An unchanged value means the other source already reported this edge. That is the entire duplicate-suppression mechanism: no timing window, no per-tick "already dispatched" flag, nothing that can leak between ticks. KeyStateManager keeps two views: A 512-bit long[] of raw key codes, so a lookup is a shift and a mask with no allocation. One boolean per action slot, which is what the edge detection runs on. The game thread and the polling thread both use it. The engine hands each of them its own instance and merges edges rather than adding a lock to the hot path. Slot to action Twelve slots, each with a press action and an optional release action: Slot Press Release --- --- --- 0 ATTACK_PRESSED ATTACK_RELEASED 1 USE_PRESSED USE_RELEASED 2 SPRINT_PRESSED SPRINT_RELEASED 3 SNEAK_PRESSED SNEAK_RELEASED 4 JUMP_PRESSED — 5 FORWARD_PRESSED FORWARD_RELEASED 6 BACK_PRESSED BACK_RELEASED 7 LEFT_PRESSED LEFT_RELEASED 8 RIGHT_PRESSED RIGHT_RELEASED 9 DROP_PRESSED — 10 SWAP_PRESSED — 11 PICK_BLOCK_PRESSED — Stage 3 — dispatch InputEventDispatcher is the single exit point. It preserves order because there is exactly one dispatcher and it is called in the order the edges were detected. public boolean submit(InputAction action, int dedupeWindowMs) { if (dedupeWindowMs > 0 && isClick(action)) { long window = dedupeWindowMs 1_000_000L; if (lastClickNanos != 0L && start - lastClickNanos = MAX_QUEUED) return false; QUEUE.offer(InputAction.Stamped.of(action, origin)); COUNT.incrementAndGet(); return true; } } ConcurrentLinkedQueue.size() is O(n), which is why the counter exists. The counter and the contents are mutated under the same lock, because a previous version incremented the counter outside the lock and a racing producer could make the queue grow past the 128 bound. Every queued action carries a capture timestamp and an origin: public record Stamped(InputAction action, long capturedAt, Origin origin) { } Origin is INPUT for a real press and REPLAY for a re-injected one. Stage 5 — the drain The drainer runs at the head of the client tick: @Inject(method = "tick", at = @At("HEAD"), require = 1) private void onTickHead(CallbackInfo ci) { Minecraft mc = Minecraft.getInstance(); if (mc.player == null) return; InputDrainer.drainAll(mc); } drainAll bails out and clears the queue when: There is no client, no player or no game mode. The mod is not active or not initialised. Safe Mode disabled the input module. A screen is open. if (dev.inputbooster.input.KeyboardRouter.isScreenOpen() (mc.gui != null && mc.gui.screen() != null)) { InputActionQueue.clear(); return; } Each action is applied inside its own guard: try { apply(stamped.action(), mc); } catch (Throwable t) { InputBoosterMod.LOGGER.warn("[InputBooster] {} failed: {}", stamped.action(), t.toString()); if (InputBoosterMod.safeMode != null) safeMode.recordError("input", t); continue; } One failing action must not abort the tick or take the client down with it. Stage 6 — suppression If the mod fired an attack this tick, vanilla must not fire a second one for the same physical click. The token is single-use and tick-scoped: public static boolean consumeAttackSuppression() { if (attackHandledTick == TICK.get()) { attackHandledTick = -1; return true; } return false; } The token carries the tick id it was issued in and is discarded when that tick ends. A missed or reordered call can never suppress a legitimate attack on a later tick. When the CPS limiter rejects an attack, the mod marks the attack as handled anyway. A blocked click stays blocked; it does not leak through as a vanilla click. The action rules The drainer is where the action semantics live. The full table is in the action reference. The rules that are not obvious: Action Rule --- --- ATTACK_PRESSED Only for a living entity within squared distance 36 ATTACK_PRESSED on a block Nothing — block breaking is a held-key mechanic that vanilla already handles every tick USE_PRESSED Only when the hit result is MISS ; a chest or a lever goes back to startUseItem() JUMP_PRESSED Only when the player is on the ground, in water, in lava or climbing SWAP_PRESSED Nothing — the offhand swap belongs to vanilla PICK_BLOCK_PRESSED Only over a block, and only if the accessor mixin applied Diagnostics DiagnosticsManager counts keyboard events, mouse events, scroll events, actions submitted, actions dropped, duplicates suppressed, repeats ignored, and the mean dispatch cost in nanoseconds. They are what the overlay's event line shows and what the Overview tab reports. They are the fastest way to tell "the event hook never fired" from "the queue was full". Related pages Architecture — the layer map. Engine modes — which source is allowed to dispatch. The queue — the bounds and the drop rules.

records.title: Engine modes
records.description: Automatic, event-driven and polled modes, how the mode is resolved, and how the compatibility fallback works.

headings.text: The mode can change at runtime

records.content: The engine has two input sources and three modes. The mode decides which source is allowed to dispatch an action; the other source still updates state. The three modes public enum Mode { AUTO("auto"), EVENT("event"), POLL("poll"); } Mode Behaviour --- --- AUTO Event hooks when they applied and no known input mod is present, otherwise polling EVENT Event hooks only. Falls back to polling when they are unavailable POLL High-rate sampling only. The hooks still update state but never dispatch The configured value maps to the mode like this: engine_mode Mode --- --- 0 AUTO 1 EVENT 2 POLL Resolving the mode CompatibilityManager.resolveMode() decides: public InputEngine.Mode resolveMode() { InputEngine.Mode configured = InputEngine.Mode.fromConfig(InputBoosterConfig.getEngineMode()); if (configured == InputEngine.Mode.EVENT && !eventSourceActive) { fallbackReason = "event hooks unavailable"; return InputEngine.Mode.POLL; } if (configured == InputEngine.Mode.AUTO) { if (!detected.isEmpty() && InputBoosterConfig.isCompatFallback()) { fallbackReason = "compatibility fallback: " + String.join(", ", detected); return InputEngine.Mode.POLL; } return eventSourceActive ? InputEngine.Mode.EVENT : InputEngine.Mode.POLL; } return configured; } eventSourceActive only becomes true after the first keyboard or mouse event actually arrives. Until then, EVENT mode falls back to polling. This is why the very first press after startup is handled by the poller even in event mode. The mode can change at runtime The mode is re-resolved in two situations: Trigger Where --- --- The first event arrives InputEngine.onKeyState calls resolveMode() again engine_mode changed in the config The client tick compares the configured value with the last one public void onKeyState(int code, boolean down) { CompatibilityManager compat = InputBoosterMod.compatibilityManager; if (compat != null) { boolean firstEvent = !compat.eventSourceActive(); compat.markEventSourceActive(); if (firstEvent) { eventDriven = true; setMode(compat.resolveMode()); } } state.setRaw(code, down); if (mode == Mode.POLL) return; ... } Even in POLL mode the event hooks still write to the state store. A mode switch therefore never starts from a stale picture, and switching is seamless. The compatibility fallback Some mods own input routing. When one of them is present and compat_fallback is on, the engine keeps polling and leaves event handling alone instead of competing for it. Detection is a class-path lookup, not a mod-list dependency, so it works the same on Fabric and NeoForge without touching loader APIs: private static final String[][] KNOWN_INPUT_MODS = { {"controlify", "dev.isxander.controlify.Controlify"}, {"midnightcontrols", "dev.lambdaurora.midnightcontrols.MidnightControls"}, {"controllable", "com.mrcrayfish.controllable.Controllable"}, {"sodium", "net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.SodiumClientMod"}, {"iris", "net.irisshaders.iris.Iris"}, {"zoomify", "com.jab125.zoomify.Zoomify"}, }; The scan runs once during initialisation. A class that cannot be loaded simply means the mod is not installed. Six mods are checked by class name. A mod that owns input routing but is not in this list will not trigger the fallback. The detection is a starting point, not a complete compatibility map. Reading the resolved mode The Compatibility tab of the settings screen shows the mode and the reason. The overlay shows the mode in its engine line, and the status line is: public String statusLine() { return "Input: " + mode.label + (eventDriven ? " (event)" : " (poll)"); } CompatibilityManager.statusLine() adds the detection result: Engine: poll sodium Turning the fallback off With compat_fallback=false , AUTO no longer downgrades to polling when an input mod is detected. It picks EVENT when the hooks are live. The fallback exists because another mod owns the event routing. Turning it off means InputBooster dispatches from hooks while that mod also dispatches from hooks, which can produce doubled or missing actions. If you turn it off, test in a world you do not mind breaking. Forcing a mode Situation Setting --- --- The hooks are not applying and you want the poller engine_mode=2 You want to prove the hooks work engine_mode=1 after the first event has fired You are not sure Leave it on 0 The mode is not part of a profile, so switching profiles does not change it. Related pages Architecture — where the manager sits. Compatibility tab — the settings side. The overlay — seeing the mode live.

records.title: Feature managers
records.description: Every feature manager, the config key that gates it, when it is ticked and what it actually changes.
records.content: Each feature is one class in dev.inputbooster.feature . Every one is ticked from the client tick and gated by a config key, by the module manager, or by both. The tick order The client tick runs the managers in a fixed order. The order matters: the CPS limiter must see the click before the counters do, and the replay must not advance while a screen is open. if (moduleManager.enabled("profiles")) perServerProfileManager.tick(client); if (moduleManager.enabled("debug")) keybindConflictDetector.tick(client); if (moduleManager.enabled("replay") && inputAllowed) replayRecorder.tick(); if (moduleManager.enabled("movement")) { sprintManager.tick(client); wTapAssist.tick(client); autoStrafe.tick(client); } if (moduleManager.enabled("anti_idle")) antiIdle.tick(client); if (moduleManager.enabled("combat")) cpsLimiter.tick(client); if (InputBoosterConfig.isBurstModeEnabled()) burstMode.tick(client); if (safeMode != null) safeMode.tick(); sessionStats.tick(currentFps, cpsLimiter.getCps()); The drain itself happens earlier, at the head of the tick, through the GameTickMixin hook. The managers Movement Class Config key What it does --- --- --- SprintManager sprint_fix , auto_sprint Sets sprinting when forward is held, not sneaking, food above 6 WTapAssist wtap_assist Multiplies horizontal velocity by 0.6 on the tick after forward is released AutoStrafeManager auto_strafe Yaw nudge of ±0.4 (40 / FPS) while sprinting below 40 FPS sprint_fix gates the whole manager. auto_sprint is only consulted inside it. Combat Class Config key What it does --- --- --- CpsLimiter cps_limiter , max_cps , cps_mode Token bucket that caps attacks per second BurstModeManager burst_mode Raises the polling rate to 1000 Hz for 60 ticks after a frame-rate drop The burst manager is ticked outside the module manager — it follows burst_mode directly. Idle and diagnostics Class Config key What it does --- --- --- AntiIdleManager anti_idle Adds 0.0001 degrees of yaw every 200 ticks EventLog event_log Bounded in-memory list of the last 80 events SessionStats — Session counters and the 60-second CPS graph LatencyProfiler — Rolling window of queue-to-drain times KeybindConflictDetector key_conflict_warn One-shot scan for two bindings on the same key DebugOverlayManager show_f3_info Owns the decision to draw the overlay OverlayRenderer , OverlayLayout overlay_ Draws the panel and places it Features Class Config key What it does --- --- --- ReplayRecorder replay_enabled Records and replays queued actions ProfileManager — Loads and saves profiles PerServerProfileManager per_server_profiles Detects the server and applies the bound profile InputClickSoundManager click_sounds Plays a UI click for executed actions Infrastructure Class Config key What it does --- --- --- ModuleManager — Runtime on/off switches for seven modules SafeModeManager safe_mode Disables a module after five errors in ten seconds ConfigTools — Import, export and presets — never called by the UI ConfigTools.applyPreset , exportConfig and importConfig are implemented and correct, but no button in the settings screen calls them. The presets pvp , low_fps , debug and the default balanced are therefore not reachable from the game. The module manager ModuleManager holds seven runtime switches: runtime.put("input", true); runtime.put("combat", true); runtime.put("movement", true); runtime.put("debug", true); runtime.put("profiles", true); runtime.put("anti_idle", true); runtime.put("replay", true); enabled() combines the runtime switch with the config: Module Also requires --- --- combat cps_limiter movement Any of sprint_fix , auto_sprint , wtap_assist , auto_strafe debug show_f3_info or event_log profiles per_server_profiles anti_idle anti_idle replay replay_enabled input Nothing — this is the execution layer itself The runtime switch is what Safe Mode flips. Safe Mode SafeModeManager counts errors per module inside a rolling ten-second window: private static final long WINDOW_MS = 10_000L; private static final int ERROR_THRESHOLD = 5; When a module crosses the threshold, only that module is disabled and the window resets. The rest of the mod keeps working. The module is re-enabled after a full quiet window, so a transient failure self-heals. The modules Safe Mode can act on are the seven the module manager knows. An error source that is not one of them — client tick , for example — is counted and reported, but it cannot grow the module manager's key set. Safe Mode disables a module. It never clears InputBoosterMod.active , so the mod as a whole stays on. Only a failed initialisation turns the whole mod off. Writing a new feature The pattern every feature follows: A volatile field in InputBoosterConfig , a getter, a setter that clamps, a line in load() , a line in save() and a line in resetDefaults() . One class in the feature package with a tick(Minecraft) method that returns immediately when the config flag is off. Create it in initialize() , tick it in onClientTick() behind the module manager. A row in the settings screen. Every control must write a real config value. Only if it should travel with a profile, and only if the field is added to the Profile record, toJson , fromJson and apply . A control that does not write a config value is a lie in the interface. The 4.1.x rework was partly about removing exactly that. If a toggle exists, it must change a file value that something reads. Related pages Architecture — the package layout. Combat and movement — the player-facing behaviour. Settings UI — how the screens are built.

records.title: Settings UI
records.description: How the InputBooster settings screens are built: the panel layout, the seven tabs, the profiles screen and the alpha warning.
records.content: The settings screen is hand-built on Minecraft's Screen API. There is no widget library and no layout engine: every row is placed by coordinate. The panel The screen draws a floating panel over the vanilla options screen rather than replacing it. Constant Value Purpose --- --- --- RAIL_WIDTH 100 The width of the tab rail HEADER_H 44 The header height, which is also the drag area MIN_PANEL_W 380 The minimum width MIN_PANEL_H 260 The minimum height The panel opens at up to 560 x 460, clamped to the window. The position is centred on the first open. int maxW = Math.max(MIN_PANEL_W, this.width - 16); int maxH = Math.max(MIN_PANEL_H, this.height - 8); panelW = savedPanelW == 0 ? Math.min(560, maxW) : clamp(savedPanelW, MIN_PANEL_W, maxW); panelH = savedPanelH == 0 ? Math.min(460, maxH) : clamp(savedPanelH, MIN_PANEL_H, maxH); Moving and resizing Gesture Result --- --- Drag inside the header Moves the panel Drag the bottom-right grip Resizes the panel, down to 380 x 260 Wheel over the content Scrolls the content Drag the scrollbar Scrolls the content The content area scrolls; the tab rail and the footer do not. Rows that do not fit the viewport are hidden rather than drawn over the header or the footer. In 4.1.0 the panel was taller than the window on a small display, and controls below the fold — including Save Close in some sections — could not be reached at all. The scrollable content area was the fix in 4.1.2-alpha. Session-only geometry The size and position are held in static fields: private static int savedPanelW, savedPanelH; private static int savedPanelX = Integer.MIN_VALUE; private static int savedPanelY = Integer.MIN_VALUE; They survive closing and reopening the screen within one session and are never written to the config file. A view preference is not a mod setting. The seven tabs private enum Tab { OVERVIEW("Overview"), KEYBOARD("Keyboard"), MOUSE("Mouse"), OVERLAY("Overlay"), PERFORMANCE("Performance"), COMPATIBILITY("Compatibility"), ADVANCED("Advanced"); } Each tab has a one-line description under its name in the rail, for example Live state, active features, session summary for Overview and Other input mods and fallback behaviour for Compatibility. Switching tabs rebuilds the widgets: switch (tab) { case OVERVIEW -> buildOverview(); case KEYBOARD -> buildKeyboard(); ... } Widgets The screen uses four custom widget types, all built in the same file. Widget Behaviour --- --- SettingSlider Integer-backed. Floats are stored as hundredths, so overlay_scale is a slider from 50 to 300 Toggle A button that flips a boolean config value Action button Runs a lambda — resync, reset counters, open the profiles screen Text row A label drawn directly, not as a widget Every widget writes a real config value through the setter, and sets hasChanges = true . A control that does not write a config value is a lie in the interface. The 4.1.x settings rework was partly about removing exactly that — which is why the inert keys are documented on the key reference page rather than hidden. Saving and closing @Override public void onClose() { if (hasChanges) InputBoosterConfig.save(); if (this.minecraft != null) this.minecraft.setScreenAndShow(parent); } The footer has two buttons: Button Behaviour --- --- Save Close Saves if anything changed, then closes Close Closes without forcing a save Because the values apply immediately, "Close" only skips the write. The file is written again at shutdown. The profiles screen ProfilesScreen is a separate screen with the same visual language: one back button, the same palette, the same row rhythm. It offers a Save button per profile, a Load button and a Delete button per profile, and a Back button. It is reached from the Advanced tab through Manage profiles . There is no button that binds a profile to a server, even though the manager can do it. And there is no event log viewer, even though the event log is collected and bounded. Both are implemented on one side only. The alpha warning screen KeyboardHandlerWarningScreen is shown before the custom keyboard handler is enabled. It exists because the handler is alpha: an untested Minecraft or mod combination can route input differently, and the handler may then pass a key twice or drop it. While the handler is on, a red line stays on the settings screen and the overlay adds a warning line. The screen router that stops a space typed in chat from becoming a jump works through the screen-tracking mixin, not through the custom handler. The alpha handler is a different, deeper change. Related pages The settings screen — the player-facing tour. Feature managers — what a control has to be wired to. Mixin inventory — the mixin that adds the options button.

headings.text: The two tests that guard the mod
Running the mod in a development client

records.content: Java 25 and a network connection for the Gradle toolchain are required. The repository builds a NeoForge jar and two Fabric jars from one core source tree. Requirements Requirement Value --- --- Java 25, set through the Gradle toolchain Network Required for the first build to fetch the toolchain and dependencies Gradle Provided by the wrapper — do not install it separately The build sets a Java toolchain explicitly: java { toolchain { languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25) } } The two Gradle builds The repository has two Gradle projects. Project Directory Loader Minecraft --- --- --- --- Root . NeoForge 26.2 Fabric fabric/ Fabric 26.3 by default Both compile the same core sources. The root project adds src/neoforge/java and one compat source set; the Fabric project adds fabric/src/main/java and its own compat source set. sourceSets { main { java { srcDirs = ['src/main/java', 'src/neoforge/java', 'src/compat/mc26_2/java'] } } } Building NeoForge, Minecraft 26.2 Fabric, Minecraft 26.3 Fabric, Minecraft 26.2 =26.2 Fabric Loader 0.19.5 mis-parses a bracket range when the Minecraft version has two components: 26.3,26.4) rejects 26.3 itself with but only the wrong version is present: 26.3! . The space-separated comparison form is parsed correctly. On Windows, use gradlew.bat instead of ./gradlew . Where the jars land Build Output --- --- NeoForge build/libs/inputbooster- -nf-mc262.jar Fabric fabric/build/libs/inputbooster- -fabric-mc263.jar The version string comes from gradle.properties and carries the loader flavour, for example 4.1.2-alpha-fabric or 4.1.2-alpha-nf-mc262 . Running the tests There are 16 test classes in fabric/src/test/java/dev/inputbooster : Test What it covers --- --- AdaptivePollRateTest The auto poll rate targets, ramp and instability clamp ComboKeyPresetsTest The Ctrl+1-5 preset values and the latch CpsLimiterTest The token bucket CpsLimiterBurstTest Burst behaviour against the bucket CpsLimiterModesTest FIXED , HUMANIZED , WEAPON_AWARE and COOLDOWN EngineConfigTest Engine mode resolution FabricDependencyRangeTest The Fabric dependency range form InputActionQueueTest The queue bound and the counter InputBoosterConfigTest Config round trips and validation InputEngineTest Edge detection across both sources LatencyProfilerTest The rolling window and the peak MixinDeclarationTest The mixin declaration rules MixinTargetSignatureTest Every hook signature against the real Minecraft jar ProfileAndReplayTest Profile capture, apply and replay behaviour SessionStatsTest The CPS buckets and the session counters SuppressionAndOriginTest The tick-scoped suppression tokens and the replay origin The changelog for 4.1.0-alpha records 81 tests in total. The config path comes from the inputbooster.configDir system property, which the tests set to a temporary folder. Nothing they write touches your real .minecraft/config . The two tests that guard the mod MixinDeclarationTest and MixinTargetSignatureTest exist because of two release-stopping crashes. MixinDeclarationTest fails the build if a registered mixin declares a non-private static method. Mixin only permits private static helpers inside a mixin, and a public one aborts the transformation of the whole target class. That bug shipped in 4.0.2-stable and crashed every client before the main menu. MixinTargetSignatureTest checks every @Inject , @Accessor and @Invoker against the resolved Minecraft jar, for both the 26.2 and 26.3 builds. It exists because 4.1.0-alpha crashed on every loader: the keyboard mixin was written against the 1.21 signature keyPress(long, int, int, int, int) while 26.2 and 26.3 use keyPress(long, int, KeyEvent) . require = 0 tolerates a missing target. It does not tolerate a handler whose parameters disagree with the target — that is a fatal injection error. The signature test is the only thing standing between a mapping change and a crash on startup. CI The gradle.yml workflow runs on pushes to main and fabric-26.2-26.3 , on tags, and on pull requests. Job What it does --- --- build-neoforge Builds the NeoForge 26.2 jar on Temurin 25 build-fabric Builds both Fabric jars from a matrix, then verifies the metadata release Publishes a GitHub release with all three jars The Fabric job verifies the dependency range form before it uploads anything: grep -q '"minecraft": ">=' /tmp/fabric.mod.json \ { echo "minecraft dependency must use the '>=x &2; exit 1; } The release job refuses to publish unless all three jars are present, derives the tag from mod_version when there is no explicit tag, and marks a release as a prerelease when the version contains alpha or beta . Running the mod in a development client Both Gradle projects define a client run configuration: ./gradlew runClient The NeoForge root project sets neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces to the mod id, so game tests in that namespace run in the development client. records.title: Action semantics
records.description: Every InputAction the mod can emit, and exactly what the drainer does with each one.
records.content: Twelve tracked bindings produce nineteen action values. The drainer decides what each one means, and several of them deliberately do nothing. The enum public enum InputAction { ATTACK_PRESSED, ATTACK_RELEASED, USE_PRESSED, USE_RELEASED, SPRINT_PRESSED, SPRINT_RELEASED, SNEAK_PRESSED, SNEAK_RELEASED, JUMP_PRESSED, FORWARD_PRESSED, FORWARD_RELEASED, BACK_PRESSED, BACK_RELEASED, LEFT_PRESSED, LEFT_RELEASED, RIGHT_PRESSED, RIGHT_RELEASED, DROP_PRESSED, SWAP_PRESSED, PICK_BLOCK_PRESSED; } Twelve have a press action, seven have a release action. The five that do not — jump, drop, swap, pick block — are one-shot actions where a release carries no information. What each action does ATTACK_PRESSED Only fires against a living entity within vanilla melee range: if (target != null && target.isAlive() && player.distanceToSqr(target) It was computed during the previous frame. That is why the drainer re-checks that the target is alive and in range instead of trusting it. A stale target would otherwise be attacked after it died or moved away. ATTACK_RELEASED Nothing. The release is tracked but not executed. USE_PRESSED Only when the crosshair hits nothing: if (hit == null hit.getType() == HitResult.Type.MISS) { mc.gameMode.useItem(player, InteractionHand.MAIN_HAND); markUseHandled(); } Condition Result --- --- Nothing under the crosshair The item is used and vanilla's use is suppressed A block under the crosshair Nothing. Vanilla's startUseItem handles it An entity under the crosshair Nothing. Vanilla handles the interaction An earlier version called useItem on every press and suppressed vanilla, so chests, levers and doors could not be opened. Now only the "right-click at nothing" case is executed, and everything else goes back to startUseItem() . USE_RELEASED Nothing. SPRINT_PRESSED / SPRINT_RELEASED case SPRINT_PRESSED -> player.setSprinting(true); case SPRINT_RELEASED -> { if (!mc.options.keySprint.isDown()) player.setSprinting(false); } On release, the mod only stops sprinting when the vanilla sprint key is also up. If the player is still holding sprint, sprinting continues. SNEAK_PRESSED / SNEAK_RELEASED The same shape as sprint, through the version shim: case SNEAK_PRESSED -> McCompat.setSneaking(player, true); case SNEAK_RELEASED -> { if (!mc.options.keyShift.isDown()) McCompat.setSneaking(player, false); } JUMP_PRESSED boolean canJump = player.onGround() McCompat.isInWater(player) player.isInLava() McCompat.isClimbing(player); if (canJump) { player.jumpFromGround(); } The jump happens one tick earlier than vanilla would. Vanilla then sees onGround() == false and does not jump a second time. The old guard required the jump key to be up , which made the branch unreachable: the event only exists because the key went down. FORWARD_PRESSED / BACK_PRESSED / LEFT_PRESSED / RIGHT_PRESSED Nothing. The mod observes them but does not move the player. Vanilla reads those keys directly. FORWARD_RELEASED Runs the W-tap helper: case FORWARD_RELEASED -> { if (InputBoosterMod.wTapAssist != null) { InputBoosterMod.wTapAssist.onWRelease(); } } The helper multiplies horizontal velocity by 0.6 on the next tick, if the forward key is genuinely up. See combat and movement. BACK_RELEASED / LEFT_RELEASED / RIGHT_RELEASED Nothing. DROP_PRESSED case DROP_PRESSED -> McVersion.dropHeldItem(player); SWAP_PRESSED Nothing, on purpose. case SWAP_PRESSED -> { // The offhand swap belongs to vanilla's own keybind path. This // used to call useItem(OFF_HAND), so pressing the swap key ate // food or placed a block instead of swapping the shield in. } PICK_BLOCK_PRESSED Only over a block, and only when the accessor mixin applied: if (mc.hitResult != null && mc.hitResult.getType() == HitResult.Type.BLOCK && mc.level != null) { if (MixinAccess.pickBlockOrEntity(mc)) { // vanilla pick-block ran } else if (!PICK_BLOCK_MIXIN_WARNED) { PICK_BLOCK_MIXIN_WARNED = true; LOGGER.warn("[Mixin] pick-block hook unavailable; pick-block input is disabled."); } } The warning is printed once per session. The summary Action Executes Condition --- --- --- ATTACK_PRESSED gameMode.attack + swing Living entity within 36 squared units ATTACK_RELEASED — — USE_PRESSED gameMode.useItem Hit result is MISS USE_RELEASED — — SPRINT_PRESSED setSprinting(true) — SPRINT_RELEASED setSprinting(false) The vanilla sprint key is up SNEAK_PRESSED setSneaking(true) — SNEAK_RELEASED setSneaking(false) The vanilla sneak key is up JUMP_PRESSED jumpFromGround() Grounded, in water, in lava or climbing FORWARD_PRESSED — — FORWARD_RELEASED W-tap velocity scale The forward key is up BACK_PRESSED / BACK_RELEASED — — LEFT_PRESSED / LEFT_RELEASED — — RIGHT_PRESSED / RIGHT_RELEASED — — DROP_PRESSED dropSelectedItem() — SWAP_PRESSED — Always vanilla's job PICK_BLOCK_PRESSED The vanilla pick-block helper Over a block, accessor applied The origin tag Every queued action carries an origin: Origin Meaning --- --- INPUT A real physical press REPLAY Re-injected by the replay recorder The origin decides three things: whether the hit counter ticks, whether the CPS graph counts it, and whether the click sound plays. A replayed event does none of those. Related pages The queue — how actions are bounded and dropped. Input pipeline — the code path. Limitations — what is not implemented.

records.title: The action queue
records.description: The bounded queue between the poller and the tick: its capacity, its locking, its drop rules and its interaction with replay.

headings.text: What happens when it is full

records.content: The queue is the boundary between two threads. It is bounded at 128 entries, lock-guarded, and every rejection is counted rather than hidden. The contract private static final int MAX_QUEUED = 128; private static final ConcurrentLinkedQueue QUEUE = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>(); private static final AtomicInteger COUNT = new AtomicInteger(0); private static final Object LOCK = new Object(); Property Value --- --- Capacity 128 entries Structure ConcurrentLinkedQueue with an explicit counter Guard One lock around every counter and content mutation Full behaviour The action is rejected and counted as dropped Clearing Used when a screen opens, when the world changes and on shutdown Why the counter exists ConcurrentLinkedQueue.size() is O(n). The counter makes the size a constant time read, which matters because the overlay and the settings screen read it while the poller is running. Why the lock exists An earlier version incremented the counter outside the lock. The polling thread could then be between its increment and its offer() when clear() ran: the polled event was lost, but the count still said "one less", so the queue could grow past 128 and defeat the bounded-backlog guarantee the architecture depends on. public static boolean queue(InputAction action, InputAction.Origin origin) { synchronized (LOCK) { if (COUNT.get() >= MAX_QUEUED) return false; QUEUE.offer(InputAction.Stamped.of(action, origin)); COUNT.incrementAndGet(); return true; } } It is uncontended apart from a few microseconds per event, and it is held only around two operations: a comparison and an offer. The stamped record public record Stamped(InputAction action, long capturedAt, Origin origin) { public static Stamped of(InputAction action, Origin origin) { return new Stamped(action, System.nanoTime(), origin); } } The capture timestamp is taken when the action is queued, which is as close to the physical press as the mod can measure. LatencyProfiler compares it with the drain time. Pending physical events public static int pendingPhysical() { synchronized (LOCK) { int physical = 0; for (InputAction.Stamped stamped : QUEUE) { if (!stamped.isReplay()) physical++; } return physical; } } The replay recorder calls this. When the number is above zero, playback holds back and rewinds its clock slightly, so a recording can never be injected on top of a live click. When the queue is cleared Moment Why --- --- A screen opens The keys belong to the screen The drainer finds a screen open Same, checked again on the game thread The world is left or reloaded Transient state must not carry into the next session The mod is not active or not initialised Nothing should execute Safe Mode disabled the input module The execution layer is off Shutdown The poller is stopped An action that is cleared is gone. It is not re-queued and it is not replayed. A tap that happened while a screen was open is simply not executed, which is correct: that input belonged to the screen. What happens when it is full The action is rejected. InputEventDispatcher.submit counts it as a dropped action and returns false. The caller does not retry — the physical press is lost. In practice, 128 entries is far more than a tick can consume unless the client is severely behind: at 1000 Hz, a tick that takes 128 ms would be needed to fill it. The replay recorder does not drop an event when the queue is full. It leaves the playback index where it is and retries on the next tick. After 20 consecutive stalled ticks — about a second — it gives up on that one event, counts it and moves on. The suppression tokens Two tick-scoped tokens live next to the queue: private static final AtomicInteger TICK = new AtomicInteger(1); private static volatile int attackHandledTick = -1; private static volatile int useHandledTick = -1; beginTick() expires the tokens from earlier ticks. A token carries the tick id it was issued in, so a missed or reordered call can never suppress a legitimate attack on a later tick. Reading the queue Source Shows --- --- The overlay Queue /128 on the dispatch line The Overview tab The queue depth InputActionQueue.size() The current count InputActionQueue.capacity() Always 128 Related pages Action semantics — what each action does. Input pipeline — the full path. Replay and logs — how replay uses the queue.

records.title: Mixin inventory
records.description: Every mixin in the mod: its target, its injection point, its require setting and what it promises.
records.content: There are ten mixins. Two observe input, one drains the queue, one tracks screens, one adds the options button, three provide accessors and two are effectively empty. The manifest { "required": true, "minVersion": "0.8", "package": "dev.inputbooster.mixin", "compatibilityLevel": "JAVA_25", "client": [ "GameTickMixin", "DebugHudMixin", "InGameHudMixin", "OptionsScreenMixin", "GuiAccessor", "KeyMappingAccessor", "KeyboardHandlerMixin", "MinecraftClientAccessor", "MouseHandlerMixin", "ScreenTrackingMixin" ], "injectors": { "defaultRequire": 1 } } Every mixin is client side. The manifest requires JAVA_25 . By default, a missing injection target fails the client at startup. A mixin that must degrade instead opts out explicitly with require = 0 on the individual injection. The critical path GameTickMixin Target: net.minecraft.client.Minecraft . Injection Point Require Purpose --- --- --- --- tick HEAD 1 Drain the queue at the start of the tick startAttack HEAD, cancellable 1 Suppress vanilla's duplicate attack startUseItem HEAD, cancellable 1 Suppress vanilla's duplicate use close HEAD 1 Shut the mod down cleanly These four are require = 1 on purpose. A mapping change must fail loudly instead of silently disabling input handling. @Inject(method = "startAttack", at = @At("HEAD"), cancellable = true, require = 1) private void onStartAttack(CallbackInfoReturnable cir) { if (!InputBoosterMod.active !InputBoosterMod.initialized.get()) return; if (InputDrainer.consumeAttackSuppression()) { cir.setReturnValue(false); } } The observers KeyboardHandlerMixin Target: net.minecraft.client.KeyboardHandler . Priority 1100. @Inject(method = "keyPress", at = @At("HEAD"), require = 0) private void onKeyPressObserved(long window, int action, KeyEvent event, CallbackInfo ci) { KeyboardProcessor.onKeyEvent(event.key(), action); } It observes. It cancels nothing, changes no binding and does no local capture. Vanilla still routes the event to the open screen, to the key bindings and to every other mod exactly as before. MouseHandlerMixin Target: net.minecraft.client.MouseHandler . Priority 1100. Injection Method Purpose --- --- --- onButtonObserved onButton(long, MouseButtonInfo, int) Turn a button press or release into an edge onScrollObserved onScroll(long, double, double) Count a wheel event, with an optional debounce Scrolling is only counted. The mod never applies scroll input to the game. require = 0 tolerates a missing target. It does not tolerate a handler whose parameters disagree with the target — that is a fatal injection error and it kills the client while the class is being transformed. This is exactly what happened in 4.1.0-alpha. The screen router ScreenTrackingMixin Target: net.minecraft.client.Minecraft . @Inject(method = "setScreenAndShow", at = @At("HEAD"), require = 0) private void onScreenShown(Screen screen, CallbackInfo ci) { KeyboardRouter.recordScreen(screen); } The 26.x API only exposes setScreenAndShow ; setScreen was removed. A hook naming it would silently never run, which is why the startup log reports which of the two the client actually has. The mixin only reads the screen argument. It does not cancel the call, does not touch key mappings and does not see another mod's input. The interface hooks OptionsScreenMixin Target: net.minecraft.client.OptionsScreen . @Inject(method = "init", at = @At("TAIL"), require = 0) private void onInitTail(CallbackInfo ci) { addRenderableWidget(Button.builder( Component.translatable("options.inputbooster.button"), button -> { ... } ).bounds(this.width - 110, 6, 100, 20).build()); } require = 0 is deliberate: this is a convenience button. A mapping change should remove the button, not stop Minecraft from starting. InGameHudMixin Target: net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui . Priority 900. @Inject(method = "extractRenderState", at = @At("TAIL"), require = 0) private void onExtractRenderStateTail(DeltaTracker deltaTracker, boolean renderLevel, boolean renderHotbar, CallbackInfo ci) { DebugOverlayManager.extractRenderState(Minecraft.getInstance()); } The signature changed in 26.x: extractRenderState(DeltaTracker, boolean, boolean) replaced the graphics-extractor overload used on 26.1. DebugHudMixin Target: net.minecraft.client.gui.components.DebugScreenOverlay . Priority 900. Intentionally empty. The class exists so the mixin list stays stable, but it injects nothing. An earlier version hooked getLeftText and getRightText , whose names differ across mapping versions, which produced "Cannot remap" warnings and an injection that never ran. The overlay now draws through the HUD render state instead, with no mapping dependency. The accessors Mixin Target Exposes --- --- --- GuiAccessor Gui The GUI render state KeyMappingAccessor KeyMapping The bound key code MinecraftClientAccessor Minecraft The vanilla pick-block helper KeyMapping , Gui and Minecraft are classes, not interfaces. An interface-form mixin for a class target aborts the transformation and kills the client during class loading. That was the 3.1.3 crash. Mixin only permits private static methods inside a mixin. A public static helper aborts the transformation of the whole target class. That was the 4.0.2-stable crash. The helpers now live in the plain class dev.inputbooster.access.MixinAccess , and MixinDeclarationTest fails the build if the rule is broken again. The rules, summarised Rule Why --- --- A critical-path injection uses require = 1 A missing hook must fail loudly An optional hook uses require = 0 A missing hook must degrade, not crash Observers run at HEAD and cancel nothing Another mod's input stays untouched Handler parameters must match the target exactly A mismatch is fatal even with require = 0 An accessor for a class target is an abstract class An interface mixin aborts the transformation A mixin contains no non-private static method A public helper aborts the transformation Accessor helpers live in MixinAccess Keeps the mixins to members only The startup check verifyClientHooks() runs during initialisation and reports what applied: [Mixin] All client hooks present. [Mixin] Screen hooks: setScreenAndShow=true, setScreen=false [Mixin] Missing vanilla method(s): tick — input handling is degraded. [Mixin] No screen hook found; screen state falls back to the HUD check each tick. The mixins use require = 0 so an API change degrades instead of crashing. Without this check, a silent failure would disable input handling with no explanation at all. Related pages Building and testing — the two tests that guard these rules. Input pipeline — where each hook sits. Limitations — the pick-block caveat.

records.title: Limitations
records.description: Everything 4.1.2-alpha does not do, including settings that are stored but have no runtime effect.

headings.text: Settings that are stored but have no effect
Features that exist but have no interface
Behaviour that is narrower than it sounds
What the mod will never do

records.content: This page lists the gaps. It is deliberately long, because a setting that looks live and is not is worse than a missing one. The alpha itself 4.1.2-alpha is the current source tree. The input engine and the new settings screen are new code and have not been tested in a running client . 4.0.3-stable is the last stable build. The repository states that the mod has not been benchmarked in a running client. No FPS figure, no latency improvement figure and no comparison with vanilla appears anywhere in this documentation, because none was measured. The internal profiler measures queue-to-drain time inside the mod, which is a different quantity. Settings that are stored but have no effect These five keys are written to the config file, validated, and reachable from the settings screen. No runtime behaviour depends on them. Key What you would expect What actually happens --- --- --- show_keystrokes A keystroke display There is no renderer. Nothing is drawn fps_check_interval FPS sampled every N ticks The adaptive rate is recomputed every client tick keyboard_repeat_guard Toggle for "a held key is one press" Repeat events are discarded unconditionally, before the toggle is read debug_mode Verbose diagnostics No log statement is gated on it click_sound_volume A quieter click sound The sound instance is created with the pitch only In every case the default behaviour is the sensible one. A held key is one press, the adaptive rate follows the frame rate, and the overlay is the only thing that draws. The problem is that the interface implies a control that does nothing. Features that exist but have no interface Feature State --- --- The event log Collected, bounded at 80 entries and correctly trimmed. No viewer. Only the internal snapshot() and latest() accessors Config import, export and presets Implemented in ConfigTools . No button calls them. The pvp , low_fps , debug and balanced presets are unreachable Per-server profile bindings PerServerProfileManager.bind() writes the file correctly. No button calls it. The binding file has to be written by hand Behaviour that is narrower than it sounds Setting Reality --- --- show_action_bar Gates the burst mode start and end messages only. The replay, profile and combo key messages are sent regardless cps_mode Never validated. An unknown value behaves exactly like FIXED , because that is the default arm of the switch mouse_scroll_debounce_ms The debounce works, but scroll is only counted. The mod never applies scroll input The overlay Has no latency average or peak line. Those values live in the profiler and are shown on the settings screen instead The action rules Some actions are deliberately narrow: Attack only fires against a living entity within 36 squared units — the vanilla melee reach. Nothing is ever attacked at a longer distance. Use only fires when the crosshair hits nothing. A chest, a lever or an entity goes back to vanilla's own startUseItem() . Block breaking is never handled by the mod. It is a held-key mechanic that vanilla already runs every tick. The offhand swap is never handled by the mod. Pick block needs the accessor mixin to have applied. If it did not, the log says so once and pick-block input is disabled for the session. Compatibility Limit Detail --- --- Six known input mods Controlify, Midnight Controls, Controllable, Sodium, Iris and Zoomify are detected by class name. A mod that owns input routing but is not on the list will not trigger the fallback The alpha keyboard handler May pass a key twice or drop it on an untested version or mod combination The event hooks require = 0 , so a renamed target degrades to polling instead of crashing. The startup log says whether they applied The screen router Falls back to a per-tick HUD check if neither screen hook applied Versions and platforms Limit Detail --- --- Minecraft 26.2 and 26.3 only No 1.21.x build exists in this tree. The 1.21 jars come from an older codebase with different behaviour No NeoForge build for 26.3 The NeoForge project targets 26.2 only Java 25 Required by the mixin manifest and by the Fabric metadata Fabric Loader 0.19.0+ The bracket-range bug in loader 0.19.5 is worked around, not fixed The archived API The public API repository is no longer maintained . It targets Minecraft >=1.21 <1.22 on Java 21 with Fabric only, and it is not wired into the 26.x tree. Anything built against it will not work with this mod. See the archived API page. Known documentation discrepancies The README and the source disagree in two places. This site documents the source. README says Source does --- --- The key bindings are in an InputBooster category They are registered under KeyMapping.Category.MISC The event mixins target MouseHandler.onPress/onScroll They target onButton and onScroll ; onPress does not exist in 26.x What the mod will never do Generate input without a physical press. Extend reach or change hit registration. Cancel another mod's key events or remap another mod's bindings. Replace vanilla's KeyboardHandler or MouseHandler . Send anything to a server that vanilla would not send. Claim a performance improvement it has not measured. Related pages Key reference — the five inert keys in context. records.title: Common issues
records.description: The failures people actually hit, what causes them and what to change.

headings.text: Typing in chat still jumps the player
Clicks feel capped below your settings
The settings screen is not reachable
The poll rate does not change
The combo keys do not work
The profile does not switch per server
The settings look reset after an update
Two InputBooster settings are different on different servers

records.content: Every issue below has a specific cause in the log. Start there rather than reinstalling. Start with the log Most problems are identified by a single line. The log reference lists all of them. The mod did not load Symptom: no InputBooster button on the options screen, no Ready! line. Cause Fix --- --- The jar does not match your Minecraft version Use the mc262 or mc263 jar that matches Two jars are installed Remove one. Two copies of the same mixins crash the client Java is not 25 Check the launcher's Java version, not the system default The loader is too old Fabric Loader 0.19.0+, Fabric API 0.161.0+, NeoForge 26.2.0.88+ The jar is in the wrong folder It must be in the instance's mods directory, not the launcher's The client crashed at launch Symptom: the game dies before the main menu. Cause Fix --- --- A mixin signature mismatch Update to 4.1.1-alpha or newer. 4.1.0-alpha crashes on every loader Two jars installed Remove one A non-private static method in a mixin Use 4.0.3-stable or newer. 4.0.2-stable crashes on every client 4.0.2-stable and 4.1.0-alpha both crash before the main menu on every client. 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 crash too, for different reasons. The jar matrix lists which published jars are unusable. Typing in chat still jumps the player Symptom: a space typed into chat moves your character. Cause Fix --- --- The screen hook did not apply Check the log for the screen hook line. At least one of setScreenAndShow or setScreen must be true No screen hook applied at all The mod falls back to a per-tick HUD check. Another mod may be feeding the player input Another mod owns input Try the alpha keyboard handler, or remove the conflicting mod The chat-jump fix comes from the screen-tracking mixin, not from the custom keyboard handler. Enable the alpha handler only after the screen hook line has been checked. Nothing works in one module Symptom: one feature stopped working; everything else is fine. Cause: Safe Mode disabled it. [SafeMode] Module 'movement' disabled after 5 errors (java.lang.NullPointerException). Fix: the module is re-enabled automatically after a quiet window. If it keeps happening, look for the error above that line — it names the exception. The mod-level switch is never cleared by Safe Mode, so the rest of the mod keeps running. Clicks feel capped below your settings Symptom: you click faster than your max_cps allows. Cause: the CPS limiter is on. Fix Effect --- --- Raise max_cps The cap rises, up to 20 Set cps_limiter=false No cap at all Change cps_mode WEAPON_AWARE caps at 16, COOLDOWN at 18 plus a minimum gap When the limiter rejects a click, vanilla's attack is suppressed for that tick. A click that the limiter blocked does not sneak through as a vanilla click. The overlay is missing Symptom: no overlay appears. Cause Fix --- --- The overlay only draws with F3 open Press F3, or set overlay_mode=1 show_f3_info is off Turn on Overlay enabled The opacity is zero Raise the opacity slider The vanilla HUD overlay option is off Enable it in the vanilla options screen The mod is not in a world The overlay needs a player The settings screen is not reachable Symptom: the InputBooster button is not on the options screen. Cause Fix --- --- The options mixin did not apply The log will show a mixin error. This is rare The window is too small The button is placed at width - 110, 6 . A very narrow window can hide it The poll rate does not change Symptom: the rate slider does nothing. Cause Fix --- --- Automatic mode is on Turn Auto off, or use the Ctrl+1-5 presets Burst mode is active The poller runs at 1000 Hz during a burst. The Overview tab shows 1000 The combo key preset did not apply Make sure no screen is open and Ctrl is held The combo keys do not work Symptom: Ctrl+1 does not change the rate. Cause Fix --- --- combo_keys is off Turn Combo keys (Ctrl+1-5) on A screen is open The combo keys are ignored while a screen is open The key is already held The chord latches: release Ctrl and the digit, then press again Replay does nothing Symptom: pressing K does nothing. Cause Fix --- --- Nothing was recorded Press R first. The log says [Replay] Nothing recorded yet. replay_enabled is off Turn it on in the Advanced tab A screen is open Playback waits until the player owns the keyboard You are pressing keys Playback holds back while real input is queued The profile does not switch per server Symptom: connecting to a server does not change the profile. Cause Fix --- --- per_server_profiles is off Turn it on in the Advanced tab There is no binding file Write inputbooster_server_profiles.properties by hand The key is not normalised Use the lower-case host with no scheme, path or port The profile name does not match The value must match a profile name exactly The binding file has to be created by hand. See profile format. The settings look reset after an update Symptom: your values came back as defaults. Cause: the config file was reset on load, or a key was not in the file. Look for this line: Config entries reset to defaults (invalid or unparsable): poll_rate_hz=2000 The named keys were reset. Every other key was applied. The full list of checked keys is in validation. Two InputBooster settings are different on different servers Symptom: a profile switch changed something you did not expect. Cause: a profile does not contain every key. Overlay geometry, the engine mode, the click dedupe and scroll debounce, and the click sound settings stay as they were. The list of excluded keys is in the key reference. records.title: Log reference
records.description: Every line InputBooster writes to the log, what it means and what to do about it.
records.content: The mod writes to the standard Minecraft log with the inputbooster logger and a [InputBooster] prefix on most lines. This page is the decoder. Startup [InputBooster] Starting v4.1.2-alpha [Mixin] All client hooks present. [Mixin] Screen hooks: setScreenAndShow=true, setScreen=false [inputbooster-config] Loading config from .../config/inputbooster.properties [inputbooster-config] ✓ Config loaded successfully (config version 305) [Input] Polling thread started at 200 Hz. [InputBooster] Ready! Line Meaning --- --- Starting v... Initialisation began All client hooks present. Every vanilla method the mod needs still exists Screen hooks: ... Which screen hook applied. At least one must be true Loading config from ... The config file was found and read Config loaded successfully The file was applied Polling thread started at N Hz. The sampler is running Ready! Everything is up If that line is present, the mod is loaded and working. Everything before it tells you which optional parts applied. Startup problems [InputBooster] Fatal init error! InputBooster is disabled for this session. Initialisation threw. The mod has disabled itself and nothing in it will work for this session. The stack trace above the line is the cause. The mod does not retry: an earlier version logged the same trace every tick and could start a second polling thread per attempt. [Mixin] Missing vanilla method(s): tick — input handling is degraded. The mod may need an update for this Minecraft version. One of the critical vanilla methods changed. The mod still runs, but part of the input path is off. [Mixin] No screen hook found; screen state falls back to the HUD check each tick. Neither setScreenAndShow nor setScreen applied. The screen state comes from the HUD instead, which is less reliable. This is the first thing to check when a space typed in chat becomes a jump. [Mixin] pick-block hook unavailable; pick-block input is disabled. The pick-block accessor did not apply. Everything else works; the pick-block key does nothing. The line is printed once per session. [Input] Could not read every key binding; using vanilla defaults for the rest. One or more of the twelve tracked bindings could not be read. The mod fell back to the vanilla default for those slots. The Keyboard tab of the settings screen reports whether all twelve resolved. Configuration [inputbooster-config] Migrating config from version 303 to 305 The file was on an older schema. Three legacy keys were renamed and the version was written back. [inputbooster-config] Config entries reset to defaults (invalid or unparsable): poll_rate_hz=2000, combo_keys=maybe One warning per load, listing every key that had to be reset. A boolean is listed by name; a number is listed as key=value . The full list of checked keys is in validation. [inputbooster-config] No config found, creating defaults... First launch. The mod writes a config file with every default in it. [inputbooster-config] Failed to load config, using defaults The file could not be read at all. The defaults are used and the game starts. [inputbooster-config] ✓ Config saved to .../config/inputbooster.properties The file was written. This happens on save and on shutdown. Input engine [Compat] Keyboard/mouse event hooks are live. The first keyboard or mouse event arrived through the mixins. From this point on, event-driven mode is available. [Input] Polling error A failure inside the poller. It is printed at most five times; the poller keeps running. A dead poller silently disables the whole mod, so the thread survives a failure on purpose. [Input] Polling thread stopped. Normal shutdown, or the poller could not start. [InputBooster] Shutting down... The mod is closing. It stops the poller, waits for it, clears the queue, saves the config and releases the keyboard. Safe Mode [SafeMode] Module 'movement' disabled after 5 errors (java.lang.NullPointerException). [SafeMode] Module 'movement' re-enabled after a quiet period. Five errors in ten seconds disabled that module. The rest of the mod kept running. The module is re-enabled automatically once the window is quiet. Safe Mode can act on seven modules: input , combat , movement , debug , profiles , anti_idle and replay . An error from any other source — the client tick, for example — is counted and logged but cannot disable a module. Features [BurstMode] FPS dropped from 120 to 80 (33%), bursting to 1000 Hz for 3s [BurstMode] Burst mode ended, returning to normal rate. Burst mode engaged and disengaged. The action bar shows the same message when show_action_bar is on. [Replay] Nothing recorded yet. [Replay] Recording stopped early: buffer full, 12 event(s) not stored. [Replay] Input queue stayed full; dropped an event from playback. [Replay] Playback finished with 1 dropped event(s). Replay problems. The first means playback was requested with an empty recording. The second means the 4000-event limit was reached. The third and fourth mean the queue was full for long enough that playback gave up on an event. [Profile] Loaded 3 profile(s) [Profile] Loaded profile: Competitive [Profile] Moved unreadable profile file to inputbooster_profiles.json.corrupt (JsonSyntaxException) Profile loading. The third line means the profile file was not valid JSON and was moved aside; the game continued with no profiles. [ServerProfile] Server detection degraded (java.lang.NoSuchFieldException); per-server profiles fall back to a stable identifier. The reflective server lookup failed. The mod keeps working with a stable identifier instead of throwing on the client tick. [Input] Key conflict detection unavailable on this Minecraft version. The key binding list could not be read through reflection, so no conflict check ran. The detector is optional. Per-action failures [InputBooster] ATTACK_PRESSED failed: java.lang.NullPointerException One action threw. It is logged, reported to Safe Mode, and the queue keeps draining. A repeating version of this line is what Safe Mode counts. [InputBooster] WTapAssist error: The W-tap helper threw while applying the velocity change. It is caught separately so it cannot abort the drain. Where the log lives Launcher Path --- --- Official .minecraft/logs/latest.log MultiMC / Prism /.minecraft/logs/latest.log Modrinth App The instance's logs folder The file is rotated at every launch. latest.log is the current session; the previous one is 2026-01-01-1.log.gz and so on.
