records.title: Diagnosing input
records.description: A systematic way to find out where an input is being lost, from the counters down to the source.

headings.text: The five places an input can be lost
Stage 1 — is the press even reaching the game?
Stage 3 — is the edge being detected?
Stage 5 — did the drainer execute it?

records.content: When an input does not arrive, the problem is always in one of five places. This page walks them in order, from the cheapest check to the deepest. The five places an input can be lost B[2. Poller or event hook] B --> C[3. Engine state] C --> D[4. Queue] D --> E[5. Drainer] E --> F[Vanilla call] A -.-> not observed B B -.-> no edge C C -.-> rejected D D -.-> cleared E E -.-> condition failed F } caption="Each stage has its own counter or log line. Start at the top." /> Stage 1 — is the press even reaching the game? Open the settings screen, go to Overview, and read the Keys and Mouse counters. Symptom Conclusion --- --- Both counters stay at zero No event is arriving. Check the log for All client hooks present. and whether the client is running the mod at all The counters rise when you press keys Events are arriving. Move to stage 2 They count every event since the mod started, including repeats and scroll. They do not reset on a screen open. Stage 2 — which source is live? The Compatibility tab shows whether the event hooks applied and which mode the engine resolved. Engine mode What it means --- --- event The hooks are live and dispatching poll The poller is the source If the mode is poll and you expected event , one of these is true: Cause Check --- --- The hooks never fired The log line Keyboard/mouse event hooks are live. is missing An input mod is installed The Compatibility tab lists it. The fallback downgrades to polling engine_mode is 1 but the hooks are not live Event mode falls back to polling until the first event proves the hooks work Stage 3 — is the edge being detected? The Overview tab's Engine row shows the mode. The overlay's counter line shows the action count: Keys 1.2k Mouse 430 Actions 880 Actions is the number of actions that were submitted to the dispatcher. Comparison Conclusion --- --- Keys and mouse rise, actions do not The event is not reaching a tracked slot Actions rise, the queue stays at 0 The actions are being drained immediately Actions rise, the queue sits at 128 The drainer is not running Only the twelve tracked bindings produce actions. A key bound to something else — a mod binding, a macro key — raises the event counters but produces no action. That is expected. Stage 4 — is the queue full? Reading Meaning --- --- Queue 0/128 Empty. Nothing is waiting Queue 127/128 or 128/128 The drainer is not keeping up, or it is not running Queue growing steadily The drainer is not running at all A full queue means new actions are rejected. The physical press is lost. Look for the drainer's failure lines in the log. Stage 5 — did the drainer execute it? The drainer runs at the head of the tick. It refuses to execute when: Condition How to confirm --- --- A screen is open The screen hook line in the log There is no player Obvious The mod is not active or not initialised The Fatal init error! line Safe Mode disabled the input module The [SafeMode] Module 'input' disabled line The per-action conditions Even when an action reaches the drainer, it may do nothing. Check the condition for that action: Action Fails when --- --- ATTACK_PRESSED The hit result is not a living entity within 36 squared units USE_PRESSED The hit result is not MISS JUMP_PRESSED The player is not grounded, in water, in lava or climbing FORWARD_RELEASED The forward key is still down PICK_BLOCK_PRESSED The crosshair is not on a block, or the accessor did not apply The action reference has the exact rule for each. The systematic checklist Ready! present? Any Fatal init error! ? Any Missing vanilla method(s) ? Any [SafeMode] line? All client hooks present. and at least one screen hook true ? Do the key and mouse counters move when you press? Is it the mode you expected? If it fell back, why? Is it empty? Is it full? Both are informative. Is the action's precondition actually satisfied in the situation where it fails? Disable the other input mods one at a time. The detector only knows six of them. A quick self-test The clearest test of the whole path: Join a world. Open the settings screen and note the Keys and Actions counters. Tap the attack key five times quickly. Watch the counters. Result Where the problem is --- --- Keys did not rise Stage 1 — the event never arrived Keys rose, Actions did not Stage 3 — the edge was not detected Actions rose, the queue stayed full Stage 4 — the drainer is not running Actions rose, the queue emptied, no attack happened Stage 5 — the action condition failed Related pages Log reference — every line. records.title: Reporting bugs
records.description: How to file a bug report that can actually be acted on, and where to file it.
records.content: A good report is short. The log file and six lines of context are worth more than a paragraph of description. Where to file Issues go to the project repository: For a security issue, use the process in the repository's SECURITY.md rather than a public issue. What to include The versions Field Where to find it --- --- Minecraft version The launcher Loader and loader version The launcher InputBooster version The jar name, or the Starting v... log line Java version java -version inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc263.jar is more useful than "the latest one", because the jar name encodes the loader and the Minecraft version. The log Attach latest.log , or paste the lines between the mod starting and the problem. The lines that matter most: Line Why --- --- Starting v... Confirms the version All client hooks present. / Missing vanilla method(s): ... Says whether the mixins applied Screen hooks: setScreenAndShow=..., setScreen=... Says whether the screen router applied Config entries reset to defaults (...) Says whether the config was reset [Compat] Keyboard/mouse event hooks are live. Says whether the event source works Any [SafeMode] line Says whether a module was disabled Any failed: line The exception that was thrown The reproduction Numbered steps that someone else can follow. The issue template asks for exactly this: To Reproduce Launch Minecraft 26.3 with Fabric Join a singleplayer world Open the InputBooster settings screen Toggle the overlay mode See the error The expected behaviour One sentence. "The overlay should stay visible when F3 is closed." The other mods List them. The compatibility detector only knows six input mods by name, so an unlisted mod is the most likely explanation for a strange input problem. Screenshots or a short clip Only for a visual or timing problem. A clip of a missed input is far more useful than a description of one. A good example Describe the bug Typing a space in chat jumps my character, even with the InputBooster options button open. To Reproduce Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 InputBooster 4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc263.jar Java 25 Join a singleplayer world Press T to open chat, type a space The player jumps Expected behaviour The space should be typed and nothing else should happen. Versions OS: Windows 11 Minecraft: 26.3 Loader: Fabric 0.19.5 InputBooster: 4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc263.jar Java: 25 Other mods: sodium 0.6.9, iris 1.7.3 Log lines [Mixin] All client hooks present. [Mixin] Screen hooks: setScreenAndShow=false, setScreen=false setScreenAndShow=false, setScreen=false means the screen router did not apply, which explains a chat-jump bug on its own. Without that line, the maintainer has to ask for the log anyway. Before you file Check Why --- --- Is it a known issue? The common issues page covers the frequent ones Is it a published jar that is known to crash? 4.0.2-stable , 4.1.0-alpha , 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 all crash at launch Does the log show Fatal init error! ? That is a mod bug — include the stack trace Does it reproduce with other mods removed? Otherwise it may be an interaction, and the report needs the other mods named Is the setting one of the five inert ones? If it is, it is a known limitation, not a regression What happens next The maintainer reads the log and the versions. A report with the log and the reproduction usually gets a diagnosis on its first reply; a report without them usually gets a request for the log. Contributing a fix If you want to fix it yourself, the contributing guide describes the branch, test and pull request expectations, and the code conventions describe the rules the mixin code has to follow.

records.title: Contribution workflow
records.description: How to propose a change, what a good pull request looks like, and what the project expects from a contributor.

headings.text: What a good pull request looks like

records.content: The project accepts bug fixes, features and documentation improvements. One change per pull request, with a description that says what changed and why. The short version A bug report with reproduction steps, or a feature proposal that explains why it is useful. A one-line bug fix can go straight to a pull request. feature/your-feature or bugfix/your-bug , from the branch that matches your Minecraft version. Clean, readable Java that follows the conventions in the repository. The code conventions page lists the rules that are not obvious. The unit suite is not enough. The engine touches vanilla behaviour, so run the game. One feature or bug per request, with a description of what changed and why. Add screenshots or a short clip if it affects visuals or gameplay. Branches The repository has two long-lived branches: Branch Target --- --- main The current Minecraft line (26.2 and 26.3) fabric-26.2-26.3 The Fabric 26.2 and 26.3 build line CI runs on pushes to both, on tags and on pull requests against main . What a good pull request looks like Requirement Why --- --- One change per request A review of three things is three reviews A description of what changed and why The maintainer needs the reason, not only the diff The unit suite passes ./gradlew test in fabric/ It was run in a client The engine's behaviour is only observable in a game Screenshots for visual changes A rendering change cannot be reviewed from a diff The mixin rules are respected A broken mixin crashes every client Two released versions crashed on launch because of mixin declaration errors. Both mistakes are now caught by a test, but only if the test is not disabled. The mixin rules These are the rules that have broken a release before: Rule Why --- --- An accessor for a class target is an abstract class An interface mixin aborts the transformation A mixin contains no non-private static method A public helper aborts the transformation The handler parameters match the target exactly A mismatch is fatal even with require = 0 A critical-path injection uses require = 1 A missing hook must fail loudly An optional hook uses require = 0 A missing hook must degrade, not crash Observers cancel nothing and change no binding Another mod's input stays untouched The full list with the reasoning is in the mixin inventory. Adding a feature The pattern every feature follows is in feature managers. The short version: a config key, a manager class, a tick hook behind the module manager, a settings control that writes a real value, and a profile field if it should travel with a profile. A toggle that does not write a config value is a lie in the interface. If a control exists, it must change a file value that something reads. Other ways to contribute The project's contributing guide also lists: Contribution What it looks like --- --- Documentation Improving the README, the guides or the wiki Testing Trying new builds and reporting what breaks Support Answering questions in the forums or Discord Code of conduct The project follows the Contributor Covenant. Be respectful and friendly. Harassment, hate speech and toxic behaviour are not tolerated. Licence By contributing, you agree that your contributions are under the same licence as the project — MIT. records.title: Code conventions
records.description: The patterns, comments and rules the InputBooster source follows, and why each one exists.

headings.text: No allocation in the hot path

records.content: The code is heavily commented, and the comments explain why rather than what . Matching that style is part of contributing here. General style Rule Example --- --- Four spaces, no tabs Standard Java Java naming conventions camelCase for fields and methods, PascalCase for types One public class per file The file name matches the class final where nothing is inherited Used on the utility classes Braces on the same line if (x) { Comments explain why A comment that restates the code is noise. A comment that records a decision is documentation. The codebase is full of the second kind: // The hit result is one frame old at tick start. // Only fire at a target that is still alive and // within vanilla melee reach. if (target != null && target.isAlive() && player.distanceToSqr(target) When a bug is fixed in place, the comment starts with FIX (...) and says what the old behaviour was. It is a short history of the decision, and it stops the next reader from re-introducing the bug. The threading rule The polling thread must never touch a Minecraft object. It reads immutable data captured on the game thread and a raw key state handle. // The thread reads immutable data captured on the game thread // and a raw key state handle, and never touches a Minecraft object. The state managers are deliberately not thread-safe: // Not thread-safe by design. The game thread and the polling thread // both use it, so the engine hands each of them its own instance and // merges edges rather than adding a lock to the hot path. Adding a lock to the hot path to make a new field safe is the wrong fix. Give each thread its own instance, or publish an immutable snapshot. No allocation in the hot path The poll loop allocates nothing: // No allocation happens per poll: the raw path reads codes directly // instead of building a snapshot object every iteration. The overlay keeps its text in a reused array and rebuilds it at most four times a second. The session statistics use a primitive ring buffer for the same reason. ConcurrentLinkedQueue.size() is O(n). The action queue keeps an explicit counter for that reason. A new hot-path call to size() is a performance regression waiting to happen. Failure handling Catch Throwable , not Exception , at the boundaries: } catch (Throwable e) { // Throwable, not Exception: a missing class or a linkage error // from a version mismatch would otherwise escape into the tick // handler on every single tick. initFailed = true; LOGGER.error("[{}] Fatal init error! InputBooster is disabled for this session.", MOD_NAME, e); active = false; } One failing action must not abort the tick: try { apply(stamped.action(), mc); } catch (Throwable t) { InputBoosterMod.LOGGER.warn("[InputBooster] {} failed: {}", stamped.action(), t.toString()); if (InputBoosterMod.safeMode != null) { InputBoosterMod.safeMode.recordError("input", t); } continue; } Config changes A new config key touches six places in InputBoosterConfig : In the appropriate group, with a comment if the value is not obvious. The setter clamps. Never trust a value that came from outside. Parsed with the matching helper, clamped inline. Written unconditionally so the file always lists every key. Otherwise the key keeps a stale value across a load. If the key should be validated and reported when it is bad. An earlier version only assigned the keys that were present in the file, so a key missing from the file kept whatever value it had in memory. Importing a partial config leaked the previous session's settings. resetDefaults() at the top of load() is what prevents that. Version differences Anything that differs between Minecraft 26.2 and 26.3 goes in src/compat/mc26_2 or src/compat/mc26_3 . Nothing version-specific belongs in the shared core. // 26.x requires an explicit swing animation component on 26.3 // and a plain hand on 26.2; the compat shim hides the difference. McVersion.swingArm(player); The build includes exactly one compat source set per target. Logging Situation Level Prefix --- --- --- Startup and shutdown info [InputBooster] or a bracketed tag A recoverable problem warn [Mixin] , [SafeMode] , [Profile] A fatal problem error [InputBooster] Log lines start with a bracketed tag so they are easy to find: LOGGER.info("[Compat] Keyboard/mouse event hooks are live."); LOGGER.warn("[SafeMode] Module '{}' disabled after {} errors ({}).", key, ERROR_THRESHOLD, error); Never log in the hot path. The counters exist instead. headings.text: 4.1.0-alpha — Input engine, new overlay, new settings

records.content: The full history, condensed. The project's own CHANGELOG.md is the authority; this page is the version-by-version summary with the practical consequences. 4.1.2-alpha — Movable, scrollable, resizable settings window The current release. Added: drag the header to move the window; drag the bottom-right grip to resize it down to 380x260; scroll the section content with the wheel or the scrollbar. The geometry is kept for the session and deliberately not written to the config file. Fixed: on a short window, controls below the fold — including Save & Close in some sections — could not be reached at all. The panel no longer covers the whole screen height. 4.1.1-alpha — Fix the launch crash in 4.1.0-alpha 4.1.0-alpha crashed during startup on every loader: InvalidInjectionException ... Invalid descriptor on inputbooster.mixins.json:KeyboardHandlerMixin The observing mixins were written against the 1.21 signature keyPress(long, int key, int scancode, int action, int modifiers) . 26.2 and 26.3 use keyPress(long window, int action, KeyEvent event) and MouseHandler.onButton(long window, MouseButtonInfo button, int action) instead of onPress . require = 0 does not protect against this. It tolerates a missing target, not a handler whose parameters disagree with the target. Fixed: the mixins target the 26.x signatures, and MixinTargetSignatureTest checks every hook against the resolved Minecraft jar for both builds. A wrong signature now fails the build instead of the game. 4.1.0-alpha — Input engine, new overlay, new settings The largest release in the 4.x line. The engine and the screens are new code and have not been run in a client. Added: The engine package: InputEngine , KeyStateManager , KeyboardProcessor , MouseProcessor , KeyBindingProcessor , InputEventDispatcher , CompatibilityManager , DiagnosticsManager and ConfigurationManager . Two observing mixins that run at HEAD, cancel nothing and use require = 0 . Engine modes with automatic fallback when a known input mod owns input routing. Diagnostics counters: keyboard and mouse events, actions submitted, rejected, duplicates suppressed, repeats ignored, mean dispatch cost. The overlay rewrite: an always-on mode, configurable content, cached text, four-corner placement with clamping. The settings redesign: seven sections in a left rail plus a separate profiles screen. Nine new config keys and schema version 305. 81 tests in total. Fixed: the overlay's text was invisible because the colours were RGB values with a zero alpha byte. The overlay only appeared with F3 open. The placement could leave the panel off-screen after a resize. Per-poll allocation was removed from the hot path. 4.0.3-stable — Launch crash fix Do not use 4.0.2-stable. It crashed before the main menu on every client. The three accessor mixins carried their cast helpers as public static methods. Mixin only permits private static methods inside a mixin, and a non-private one aborts the transformation of the whole target class: InvalidMixinException: Mixin inputbooster.mixins.json:KeyMappingAccessor contains non-private static method boundCode(Lnet/minecraft/client/KeyMapping;)I That ran while the game was loading Minecraft , so the launch ended with "Mixin transformation of net.minecraft.client.Minecraft failed" and no crash report. The helpers moved to the plain class dev.inputbooster.access.MixinAccess . A regression test, MixinDeclarationTest , now fails the build if any registered mixin declares a non-private static method. 4.0.2-stable — Withdrawn Kept for history. Crashes on launch; use 4.0.3-stable. 4.0.2-alpha — Alpha keyboard handler Added: the custom keyboard handler, off by default. KeyboardRouter makes the screen decision from the game's own show-screen call instead of asking the HUD at tick time. ScreenTrackingMixin only observes that call. Fixed: a space typed in chat jumped the player, because the poller read raw key state at full rate with no reliable screen signal. 4.0.1-beta — Input pipeline correctness pass A bug review of the whole input path. No new features. Fixed, among about twenty items: Bug Fix --- --- COOLDOWN CPS mode allowed one click per session The minimum gap was computed in nanoseconds and multiplied by 1,000,000 again, giving roughly 15 hours. It is now 35 ms or one window divided by the cap Clicks inside a screen executed in the world The poller and the drainer now require that no screen is open Right-click ignored block interaction Only the "nothing under the crosshair" case is executed now The swap-offhand key used the offhand item The swap is vanilla's job One failing action could crash the tick Every action is applied inside a guard, and the queue keeps draining Jump from the mod never ran The old guard required the jump key to be up, which made the branch unreachable Fallback sprint and sneak keys were swapped The defaults now match vanilla A failed init retried on every tick Initialisation stops after one failure Keys held through a pause fired fresh presses on resume The state is re-read instead of cleared Entity attacks could target a stale hit result The target is re-checked for life and reach Replay inflated session stats Only physical input ticks the counters now The overlay scale did not reach the text The glyphs are scaled too 3.1.4 — Mixin declaration fix The 3.1.3 jars could not start the client at all: InvalidMixinException: @Mixin target type mismatch: net.minecraft.client.KeyMapping is not an interface The three accessors were declared as interface mixins, but their targets are classes. All three are now abstract class mixins, and the casts moved into static helpers that return a fallback when the mixin is not applied. 3.1.3 — Loader compatibility fix Every 3.1.2 Fabric jar crashed on launch: requires version 26.2,26.3) of 'Minecraft', but only the wrong version is present: 26.2! The metadata declared a bracket range that Fabric Loader 0.19.5 evaluates incorrectly for a two-component version. The fix was the space-separated form >=26.2 The current jars declare >=26.3 3.1.2, 3.1.1, 3.1.0 — The first 26.x line The first releases for Minecraft 26.2 and 26.3. 3.1.2 is unusable because of the range bug above. 3.0.2-rl1 — Minecraft 1.21.11 The production release of the 1.21 line. A different codebase with a different configuration layout, different key binds and a different engine. Nothing in this documentation describes it. Related pages [Jar matrix — which jar to install. Support matrix — the version ranges. Versioning — how the numbers work.

records.title: Versioning
records.description: How InputBooster version numbers, jar names and the config schema version relate to each other.
records.content: There are three different version numbers in this project: the mod version, the config schema version and the Minecraft version. They are unrelated and are easy to confuse. The three versions Version Example Where it lives --- --- --- The mod version 4.1.2-alpha The jar name and InputBoosterMod.MOD_VERSION The config schema 305 config_version in the properties file The Minecraft version 26.2 , 26.3 The mc262 / mc263 suffix and the dependency ranges 4.1.2-alpha writes config_version=305 . The two numbers are unrelated. The schema version only changes when the meaning of a config key changes. The mod version scheme MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-PRERELEASE │ │ │ │ │ │ │ └─ alpha, beta, or nothing for a stable release │ │ └────────── the patch number │ └──────────────── the minor number └─────────────────────── the major number Stage Meaning --- --- alpha New or rewritten code. May crash, may not have been run in a client beta Feature complete for the line, still being tested Stable No suffix. A release that has been tested and does not crash on launch The current release is 4.1.2-alpha . The last stable build is 4.0.3-stable . The 4.1.x line contains a rewritten input engine and a rewritten settings screen. Both are new code that has not been tested in a running client. The repository itself recommends 4.0.3-stable until the alpha has been tested. The jar name inputbooster- - -mc .jar inputbooster-4.1.2-alpha-fabric-mc263.jar │ │ │ │ │ │ │ └─ 263 = Minecraft 26.3 │ │ └────── mc │ └───────────── fabric or nf └────────────────────────── the mod version The loader flavour is also in gradle.properties : Project Property Value --- --- --- NeoForge mod_version 4.1.2-alpha-nf-mc262 Fabric mod_version 4.1.2-alpha-fabric The Fabric project appends the Minecraft suffix at build time: version = "${mod_version}-mc${minecraft_version.replace('.', '')}" The NeoForge project hardcodes the Minecraft suffix in gradle.properties , because it builds one target. The Fabric project builds both, so it derives the suffix from the minecraft_version property. The config schema version config_version records the shape of the config file. Schema Introduced Change --- --- --- 305 4.1.0-alpha Nine new engine and overlay keys 303 and earlier 3.x Older schema, migrated on load The schema version is bumped when a key changes meaning, not when a key is added for a new feature in a way that is backwards compatible. The migration is small on purpose: it renames three legacy keys and nothing else. public static final int CONFIG_VERSION = 305; The migration writes the new version back into the properties object, and the file is written again on the next save. A migrated file stops migrating. How a release is cut The CI pipeline publishes a release when a version tag is pushed, or on a branch push. From the tag, or from mod_version in gradle.properties with the loader flavour stripped. NeoForge 26.2, Fabric 26.2 and Fabric 26.3, each on Temurin 25. The release job refuses to publish unless all three are present. The Fabric job checks the dependency range form first. All three jars are attached, the notes are generated from the git log since the previous tag, and a prerelease flag is set when the version contains alpha or beta . A branch push skips the release if the tag already exists, so pushing to main twice does not publish two releases. The archived API version The API repository has its own version line, ending at 3.1.0 . It targets Minecraft >=1.21 <1.22 and Java 21, and it is not connected to the 26.x tree. See the archived API page. Related pages Changelog — what changed in each release. Support matrix — which versions are supported. Updating — moving between versions.

headings.text: How it was meant to be wired in

records.content: There are two repositories with the InputBooster name. The mod and this documentation come from one. The API is a separate, archived project that is not connected to the current tree. Its status The API repository's own README opens with the conclusion: InputBooster API - No Longer Maintained Maintenance has ended. This repository is no longer actively developed or supported. It is preserved for reference only. A dependency on dev.inputbooster:inputbooster-api:3.1.0 will not work with the 4.1.x mod. The API targets Minecraft >=1.21 What it targeted Property The archived API The current mod --- --- --- Minecraft >=1.21 The current source tree contains no dev.inputbooster.api package, no InputBoosterAPI class and no InputBoosterAPIImpl . The implementation stub was never merged into the 26.x tree. Why it is not connected Reason Detail --- --- The Minecraft version moved The API is pinned to 1.21.x. The mod is 26.2 and 26.3 The Java version moved The API needs Java 21. The mod needs Java 25 The engine was rewritten The 4.1.0 engine introduced InputEngine , a new state machine and new diagnostics. The API's surfaces do not map onto it Maintenance ended The repository states it should not be assumed to receive compatibility updates What to use instead You want to… Use --- --- Read live input statistics The overlay and the Overview tab of the settings screen Change a setting from another mod The config file, or the settings screen React to input events There is no public event API in 4.1.2-alpha Build a profile The profiles screen and inputbooster_profiles.json Read the latency figures The profiler and the session statistics The current mod has no supported way for another mod to observe its input events. If you need that, the options are to contribute a listener surface to the mod, or to read the diagnostics counters. The contribution guide covers the first option.
